raw_summary: Nissan Motor India Pvt Ltd (NMIPL) has just announced a compelling and attractive festive offer for Nissan buyers. These Government approved CNG retrofit kits for Magnite and Gravite cost Rs 85,999 and Rs 74,999, respectively. And for a limited period of time, Nissan is offering these CNG retrofit kits at no extra cost for Magnite and Gravite buyers.

As per the Nissan India’s new festive offer, Magnite and Gravite buyers can avail Government approved retrofit CNG kits for free. This limited time festive offer is only applicable on select Magnite and Gravite variants and booked before 16th of November, 2026.

The eligible variants are all non-Turbo versions of Nissan Magnite excluding VISIA MT, VISIA EZ-SHIFT and VISIA+ MT). Where Nissan Gravite is concerned, eligible variants are of TEKNA trim. These Government approved retrofit CNG kits come with third party warranty of 3 years or 1,00,000 km (whichever is early) on top of standard vehicle warranty.

It has to be noted that CNG retrofit kit for Magnite would otherwise cost Rs 74,999 and it is s single-cylinder setup in the boot. Gravite, on the other hand, gets a slightly more sophisticated CNG retrofit kit, otherwise priced at Rs 85,999, is split between two cylinders (2 X 25 litres), so that it retains the functionality of three row seating.

This limited period festive offer by Nissan on Magnite and Gravite reflects the company’s focus on making practical and economical mobility more accessible to Indian families. Offering CNG retrofit kits worth up to Rs 86k also promotes green fuels and overall reduction of carbon footprint on the environment.

After the festive offer ends, these CNG retrofit kits will retain their original price of Rs 75k for Magnite and Rs 86k for Gravite, like before. The company has not announced any other additional festive benefits with Magnite and Gravite.

title: Ferrari's engine weakness hides biggest Vasseur success
raw_summary: Ferrari’s 2026 will be remembered for the counterproductive battles between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, the 18th season of its record Formula 1 title drought and snatching defeat from the jaws of victory several times. These are all justifiably big storylines, but they shouldn’t bury the lede that team principal Fred Vasseur’s revolution has made measurable progress that, factoring in an engine deficit that he says the team long knew would hold it back in 2026, means that in the Ferrari SF-26 it has produced arguably the best chassis.

article_paragraphs: Ferrari’s 2026 will be remembered for the counterproductive battles between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, the 18th season of its record Formula 1 title drought and snatching defeat from the jaws of victory several times.

These are all justifiably big storylines, but they shouldn’t bury the lede that team principal Fred Vasseur’s revolution has made measurable progress that, factoring in an engine deficit that he says the team long knew would hold it back in 2026, means that in the Ferrari SF-26 it has produced arguably the best chassis.

Ferrari has consistently shipped time to its rivals on the straights, and has been most competitive on tracks with plenty of traction-limited content, for example the Hungaroring - and at altitude at Mexico City, where this engine disadvantage is mitigated.

The car is impressive in the corners, and while it would be overstating the case to say that this is universally the case rather than being a general trend, there’s little doubt that it would be a big threat to Mercedes, and possibly its superior on that front.

Vasseur took over as Ferrari team principal at the start of 2023. At times, he's been a beleaguered figure plagued by inevitable rumours about his replacement flaring up and frustrated by the occasions when his drivers get in each other's way. His avuncular manner shrouds a steeliness that has brought success across motorsport.

Quietly, he made some progress in rebuilding Ferrari’s long-lost winning culture, although this remains a work in progress. That task is complicated by the relentless scrutiny of the Italian media, which regards Ferrari as more than an F1 team. Gazzetta dello Sport, Italy’s largest sports daily, even used Kimi Antonelli’s world title to attack Ferrari on its front page.

It’s fair to criticise Vasseur for the concerning pattern of drivers not being entirely co-operative on track, given he is the boss and the buck stops with him. But knowing the way he works, it’s impossible to shake the feeling that his hands may be tied by those above.

Maybe that’s now changed. There are also times when he could perhaps play the media game, in Italy in particular, a little better, although it might be that’s an unwinnable fight it's best not to get drawn into. The only way to do that is results. And although two wins so far this year is a failure by Ferrari standards, the trajectory is positive.

title: New TVS iQube With Android Auto Debuts At EICMA 2026
raw_summary: TVS Motor set up a grand pavilion at EICMA 2026 in Milan, Italy and at this stage, the company announced their portfolio for Europe. The electric lineup included M1S, which will first launch in Indonesia and then in Europe, followed by TVS X, and then Orbiter. Making some noise on the stage was the unveiling of TVS RTR 125 which stole the show, basically. However, at the same stage, TVS Motor announced something in a passing glance and was even displayed on the screen for just a short while, which grabbed our attention. That is the announcement that TVS iQube electric scooter will soon get Android Auto, in partnership with Google.

article_paragraphs: TVS Motor set up a grand pavilion at EICMA 2026 in Milan, Italy and at this stage, the company announced their portfolio for Europe. The electric lineup included M1S, which will first launch in Indonesia and then in Europe, followed by TVS X, and then Orbiter. Making some noise on the stage was the unveiling of TVS RTR 125 which stole the show, basically.

However, at the same stage, TVS Motor announced something in a passing glance and was even displayed on the screen for just a short while, which grabbed our attention. That is the announcement that TVS iQube electric scooter will soon get Android Auto, in partnership with Google.

Currently, top variants of iQube get a 7-inch touchscreen that supports a host of connected attributes and smart features. This touchscreen will now support Android Auto for the first time. It will be the same Android Auto interface that we are familiar with in cars and the 7-inch screen real estate should not pose any limitations, where size is concerned.

TVS Motor announced that they have partnered with Google to offer Android Auto connected feature with their popular iQube scooter. The same cluster also shows vehicular details too. These include battery SOC, range computer, trip computer, speedo clock and more. There are tell-tale signs integrated in the same display too.

It has to be noted that TVS Motor has worked with Google before and TVS X for India already gets wireless Android Auto integration in its 10.2-inch TFT instrument cluster. Same feature will also be offered with the TVS X for European market as confirmed by the company on the same stage.

With Android Auto, users will now be able to access the same apps from their phone instead of using proprietary apps to get things done. The company did not explain whether the connection is wireless or wired. Also, there was no announcement whether this feature will be offered starting now with new buyers or can be unlocked to existing customers as well.

There was no announcement of Apple CarPlay with iQube yet. It makes sense for TVS Motor to just stick with Android Auto owing to the sheer proportion of Android user base in India, as opposed to iPhones.

raw_title: How does Oahu get to an economically resilient, 100% clean energy future?
title: How does Oahu get to an economically resilient, 100% clean energy future?
raw_summary: Oahu is a unique place. It’s the home of one of the largest clean tech incubators in the world, Elemental Impact, for a reason. Exorbitantly high electricity rates combined with ample natural resources make it an incredible laboratory to bring clean tech solutions to market. Rapid investment for WWII created a grid that was dependent on foreign oil. Path dependency (the idea that “what you know” becomes what you continue to do) hampered innovation and resulted in the creation of infrastructure (multiple power plants across multiple islands) that still, today, burns diesel fuel as large generators, to produce electricity for the island. Throw in a dependence on imported fuels that must come at least 3,000 miles to arrive, being the strategic hub for the entire Pacific theater of the U.S. military, one of the wildest weather years and hurricane seasons the island chain has ever seen AND the state’s economic dependency on tourism dollars, high cost of living, and low wages, and and wow – you’ve got yourself a puzzle and a half to solve in order to get the place to a sustainable future. Analyst Mike Barnard loves a challenge, so he set forth to put together a roadmap to help Oahu get to 100% clean energy , which helps recirculate money in the state, lower costs, create jobs and foster economic resiliency.

article_paragraphs: Oahu is a unique place. It’s the home of one of the largest clean tech incubators in the world, Elemental Impact, for a reason. Exorbitantly high electricity rates combined with ample natural resources make it an incredible laboratory to bring clean tech solutions to market. Rapid investment for WWII created a grid that was dependent on foreign oil. Path dependency (the idea that “what you know” becomes what you continue to do) hampered innovation and resulted in the creation of infrastructure (multiple power plants across multiple islands) that still, today, burns diesel fuel as large generators, to produce electricity for the island. Throw in a dependence on imported fuels that must come at least 3,000 miles to arrive, being the strategic hub for the entire Pacific theater of the U.S. military, one of the wildest weather years and hurricane seasons the island chain has ever seen AND the state’s economic dependency on tourism dollars, high cost of living, and low wages, and and wow – you’ve got yourself a puzzle and a half to solve in order to get the place to a sustainable future.

Analyst Mike Barnard loves a challenge, so he set forth to put together a roadmap to help Oahu get to 100% clean energy , which helps recirculate money in the state, lower costs, create jobs and foster economic resiliency.

Recently I gave a talk at Hawaii Tech Week in which I summarized this report, added in my own experience running an energy efficiency service that has now greened more than 20,000 homes and is saving Hawaii residents over $10 million a year on their utility bills, and then compiled the new and coming technologies that can help the island get off fossil fuels.

Mike’s report did something very important. The state’s own reporting and strategy looks at the big picture, a very difficult mountain to climb. Mike looked at that mountain and removed some of the false summits and unachievable viewpoints, resulting in a much more achievable and strategic pathway. What he did was eliminate the things we simply cannot fix right now – long distance flights, maritime bunkering, and military fuels – and tackled the problem of Oahu’s actual energy consumption for its residents. The result was that it was achievable, and there are technologies right now today that can be deployed in what he refers to as a “no regret stack” first and foremost.

I combined that with my approach, which was to showcase the economic resilience it creates. Case in point, an LED bulb saves so much money on Oahu that it pays for itself in 18 days. Every day after that, it is like change plinking in a piggy bank for the person who put it in. That builds economic resiliency for those who need it most. From LEDs to e-bikes to heat pump water heaters to balcony solar – it all adds up – fast payback periods, and financial independence.

Mike comes back to the things we simply can’t fix right now and argues that the tech will come – but for the duration of the 2020s and into the 2030s, we should be installing parking lot solar canopies, agrivoltaics, heat pump water heaters, and more.

title: China Truck Sales Now Majority Electric. What's Next?
raw_summary: EV heavy trucks hit 50.3% market share in China for September, with sales up 34% from a year ago. Long-haul big rig market share hit 64.5%. China is on track to have over 40% EV market share for the entire year, reaching their 2030 goal in a matter of months. This is not the first time China’s heavy truck market share topped 50%, but that previous blip in December last year was prior to subsidies ending, followed by a dip in January. Current sales rates are not bolstered by the subsidy and are now on a much more stable upward trajectory. When I visited Guangzhou in November of last year and again in April of this year, I noticed a lot more green plates on trucks, indicating that they were electric. It seems that my perception is backed by sales data.
summary: EV heavy trucks hit 50.3% market share in China for September, with sales up 34% from a year ago. Long-haul big rig market share hit 64.5%. China is on track to have over 40% EV market share for the entire year, reaching their 2030 goal in a matter of months.
article_paragraphs: EV heavy trucks hit 50.3% market share in China for September, with sales up 34% from a year ago. Long-haul big rig market share hit 64.5%. China is on track to have over 40% EV market share for the entire year, reaching their 2030 goal in a matter of months. This is not the first time China’s heavy truck market share topped 50%, but that previous blip in December last year was prior to subsidies ending, followed by a dip in January. Current sales rates are not bolstered by the subsidy and are now on a much more stable upward trajectory.

The speed of EV adoption for heavy trucks in China has recently grown much faster than for cars, having risen from just 13.6% in 2024. When I visited Guangzhou in November of last year and again in April of this year, I noticed a lot more green plates on trucks, indicating that they were electric. It seems that my perception is backed by sales data.

With the addition of LNG trucks, diesel’s share of heavy trucks has dropped to roughly 40%. While LNG sales have also declined with the rate of EV adoption, diesel trucks could soon make up less than 1/3 of sales and decline further from there. China could feasibly double its 2030 goal and hit 80% EV penetration, by which point many diesel models are likely to be discontinued.

With these levels of market penetration, in addition to retirements, China’s diesel demand is on track to fall by about 230,000 barrels per day this year, despite increased freight movement. Every additional electric truck that replaces a diesel truck then builds on that reduction. Due to their duty cycle, each electric truck sold has a much greater impact on fuel consumption than each car sold. And the price of fuel combined with the duty cycle has a much greater impact on overall truck economics.

To be clear, these improving results are not due to subsidies, as they appear in the year after subsidies were cut. They are also not due to mandates, as the 2030 goals were met before the ink was dry on their announcement. EV trucks are now more affordable to own and operate than diesel trucks in China. The increase in diesel prices has only increased the cost gap.

Last year, roughly 90% of all electric truck sales globally were in China. That percentage is set to expand this year, despite rising sales in some other countries. Those sales are simply not rising fast enough outside of China to keep pace with China. In comparison, the EU is looking at 2.5% EV market share this year. China is on pace to average roughly as many electric trucks sold per week as Europe sells per year. The US EV truck market looks like a rounding error in comparison at less than one percent.

In addition, China has rapidly been building out heavy truck charging infrastructure as part of the 28 million charging facilities planned to be in operation by the end of 2027, up from 21 million last March. This not only focuses on the major cities but also extends into more rural areas that have been slower to adopt electrification. In addition, several companies are building out battery swap stations. While we have yet to see if battery swap or MW+ charging wins in the truck market, expect the competition between the two approaches to be fierce.

Within Tier 1 cities, I could see a potential phase out of diesel trucks in the near future. Hainan province is already planning to end ICE passenger car sales by 2030 , and I expect that to extend to diesel trucks as well. Although rural areas have been slower to adopt, they also tend to be less wealthy and thus more impacted by the changing economics. If diesel prices stay elevated while charging becomes convenient, many rural businesses will not be able to afford to buy new diesel trucks. With the end of diesel truck sales, strict emissions standards and a potential return of scrappage incentives could take remaining diesel vehicles off the road at an accelerated rate.

title: Stratos Data Center Will Emit Air Pollution That's Linked to Premature Deaths and Health Economic Damages for Utah & States Downwind

article_paragraphs: A new report models emissions from different on-site methane generation power scenarios to show potential impacts on the people of Utah and residents of multiple downwind states.

Canadian businessman and television personality “Mr. Wonderful” (aka Kevin O’Leary) and his businesses have proposed the Stratos data center in Box Elder County, Utah, near Salt Lake City, that will be one of the largest data centers in the world, requiring as much as 9 gigawatts (GW) of on-site power from burning methane gas. The Box Elder County Commission approved the project in May— under highly contentious circumstances and under a highly unusual arrangement within a project area created by Utah’s Military Installation Development Authority.

A new report prepared by EmPower Analytics Group for NRDC estimates that the air pollution, health harms, and economic damages from the proposed Stratos data center would be substantial: “[a]t the potential 9 GW full build-out, air pollution from Stratos’s methane-gas power generation is estimated to cause approximately 5–45 additional premature deaths and $75–$690 million in health-related economic damages every year.” The report also discusses additional health harms that extend beyond premature deaths and include new asthma cases, nonfatal heart attacks, hospital visits, and lost work and school days.

These ranges reflect scenarios that model the health harms and economic damage caused by air pollution from two possible methane-gas primary power generating technologies: modern combined-cycle combustion turbines and methane gas–fired reciprocating internal combustion engines (RICE). The primary harmful air pollution consists of tiny soot particles— particulate matter of 2.5 microns or less (PM2.5) —about 30 times smaller than the width of an average human hair.

The report further finds that over a 30-year period, at the potential 9 GW full build-out, the health and economic harms from this PM2.5 air pollution “could accumulate to approximately 856–1,350 premature deaths and $13.5–$20.7 billion under gas-fired RICE, compared with 145–253 premature deaths and $2.3–$3.8 billion under combined-cycle gas.”

Of the two methane-gas primary power generation technologies evaluated in the report, one uses a smaller number of large gas combustion turbines, while the RICE scenario reflected electricity generated by many individual engines operating in parallel. Indeed, the RICE scenario is patterned on a methane gas–powered data center with 69 RICE generators that the Utah Division of Air Quality permitted in Millard County in early 2026. RICE generators produce higher emissions than combined-cycle gas at the same generation capacity. Accordingly, the report finds that “[t]he technology used to power Stratos could make a five- to sixfold difference in its estimated health harms.”

Importantly, the modeled combined-cycle gas scenario does not estimate the emissions from the use of on-site diesel generators for backup power because those plans by Stratos remain unknown. (The report modeled diesel backup generators for the RICE scenario, scaled from the Millard County permit example.) Diesel generators are significantly dirtier than comparably sized methane gas generators, emitting 95 percent more smog-forming nitrogen oxides than an equivalent gas generator as well as 98 percent more non-methane hydrocarbons and 59 percent more carbon monoxide. Harmful PM2.5 emissions will be even higher from any data center employing diesel generators (the scale of that additional pollution would depend on whether they were truly used for “emergency conditions” versus being run more frequently; state permitting parameters for backup diesels is a critical issue for all data center developments).

The highest concentrations of harmful air pollution from the Stratos data center will occur near the facility in Box Elder County, neighboring areas of northern Utah (including Salt Lake City), and southern Idaho. For decades, climate policy has been dominated by a central question: How do we avoid exceeding 1.5 degrees Celsius of global warming above preindustrial levels?
article_paragraphs: As the world is on track to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius of global warming, climate action must double down but also go beyond emissions cuts to prioritize adaptation, respond to loss and damage, and confront growing inequality.

For decades, climate policy has been dominated by a central question: How do we avoid exceeding 1.5 degrees Celsius of global warming above preindustrial levels? An overshoot world—where warming exceeds 1.5 degrees Celsius before potentially declining—means more than higher temperatures; it means escalating risks to the communities, ecosystems, and species already bearing the brunt of climate change, with catastrophic consequences for many coastal regions and small island states.

The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) report on climate overshoot challenges us to confront a reality that many policymakers have been reluctant to fully acknowledge: The world will exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius. Decades of insufficient climate action have placed us in this predicament.

Aggressive emissions reductions can limit how far and for how long global warming exceeds that threshold. However, a future decline in global temperatures would not erase the losses experienced along the way. That reality should sharpen global climate ambition and broaden our understanding of what climate action requires. It is equally important to prepare for and respond to the escalating impacts that communities and ecosystems will experience in the decades between crossing 1.5 degrees Celsius and hopefully returning to a temperature below it.

One of the UNEP report’s central messages is that mitigation and adaptation are fundamentally intertwined, and both will be essential in navigating an overshoot world. The report also emphasizes the growing need for transformational adaptation : actions that go beyond incremental adjustments to fundamentally reshape systems, institutions, and development pathways in response to escalating climate risks.

Yet there is an alarming disconnect between the scale of adaptation that is needed and the reality on the ground. Many countries are still struggling to finance and implement basic adaptation measures. Adaptation finance remains grossly inadequate, national adaptation plans are underfunded, and frontline communities continue to lack the resources needed to prepare for worsening risks. The Adaptation Gap Report 2025 estimated adaptation finance needs in developing countries at up to US$365 billion per year by 2035, while international adaptation finance flows from developed countries reached just US$35 billion in 2024 , only around 10 percent of what is needed.

There is reason for optimism. After decades of advocacy, adaptation is finally receiving greater recognition as a core pillar of climate action. Negotiations on the global goal on adaptation (GGA)—which aims to enhance adaptive capacity, strengthen resilience, and reduce vulnerability—have elevated adaptation within international climate discussions. Initiatives such as the Fostering Investable National Implementation (FINI) are also helping to mobilize public and private investments to scale adaptation efforts.

What happens when livelihoods—particularly those connected to our food system—become untenable because of chronic drought, extreme heat, or repeated disasters? What happens when infrastructure designed for one climate must function in a dramatically different one; when transit and energy hubs become inoperable due to heat? What happens when fundamental changes in land use become unavoidable, and our forests and farmlands can’t keep up with those changes?

title: If The US Department Of Defense Gets Solar Power, Why Can't We?
raw_summary: In the topsy-turvy world of today’s federal energy policy, solar power is a bad thing. Various members of the President’s cabinet have advised that solar is “unreliable,” and that solar power plants routinely experience “catastrophic failure” with every sunset . So why does the US Department of Defense continue to pursue solar-enabled microgrids at its facilities? summary: In the topsy-turvy world of today’s federal energy policy, solar power is a bad thing. Various members of the President’s cabinet have advised that solar is “unreliable,” and that solar power plants routinely experience “catastrophic failure” with every sunset . So why does the US Department of Defense continue to pursue solar-enabled microgrids at its facilities?
article_paragraphs: In the topsy-turvy world of today’s federal energy policy, solar power is a bad thing. Various members of the President’s cabinet have advised that solar is “unreliable,” and that solar power plants routinely experience “catastrophic failure” with every sunset . So why does the US Department of Defense continue to pursue solar-enabled microgrids at its facilities? Asking for a friend…

Though some solar projects at military facilities are relatively small, they are stamped with the seal of approval from the Defense Department, and that can have an outsized influence on public perceptions about the reliability, security, and durability of photovoltaic systems.

The history-making White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico is a case in point. In February of 2025 the facility celebrated the launch of a new, 700-kilowatt solar array designed and built by the joint venture HSGS-Ameresco.

At 700 kW, the new array is peanuts compared to the megawatt scale common among modern solar power plants. However, a little can go a long way in some cases, particularly when solar is integrated with other energy resources in a microgrid that can operate independently, without interruption, if the local distribution grid goes down.

“The innovative microgrid system, which integrates a 700kW solar photovoltaic array, a 500kW natural gas generator, and a 500kW lithium-ion battery system, will provide backup power to four groundwater wells on the range,” Ameresco explained in a press statement last year, in which it described the White Sands project.

The four wells are the primary source of potable water to the main post at White Sands. The new microgrid meets a US Army requirement for up to 14 days of independent water and power delivery to the post in case of a grid outage.

“This self-sufficient energy system, designed to serve a specific geographic area, helps ensure that critical missions at WSMR can proceed without interruption,” Ameresco elaborates, adding that the microgrid underscores White Sands’s commitment to building more resilient energy systems into its future construction projects.

Ameresco also indicated that the now-familiar combineation of solar power and BESS (battery energy storage systems) will do most of the heavy lifting, with the gas generator playing a back-up role if necessary.

A long single-piece seat includes a raised pillion section, accompanied by split grab handles. Handguards, conventional mirrors, separate indicators and a rear wheel-mounted plate holder add functional details to the prototype.
The tank-shaped upper enclosure also features a keyed lock with “vault open” lettering, suggesting provision for an accessible compartment. Its purpose and capacity have not been confirmed.
A substantial finned enclosure occupies the centre and lower portion of the motorcycle. Sculpted side panels carry “Air Duct” markings, indicating that airflow management forms part of the design.

title: Herta gets another Cadillac F1 practice to earn superlicence
raw_summary: Cadillac will give Colton Herta another practice outing at the Brazilian Grand Prix to earn him the last point he needs to finally secure his Formula 1 superlicence. This will be Herta's sixth FP1 outing of the season with Cadillac and he'll replace Sergio Perez. The team only needed to do four to satisfy the rookie practice requirements - but Herta's still short of the 40 superlicence points needed.
summary: Cadillac will give Colton Herta another practice outing at the Brazilian Grand Prix to earn him the last point he needs to finally secure his Formula 1 superlicence. This will be Herta's sixth FP1 outing of the season with Cadillac and he'll replace Sergio Perez.
article_paragraphs: Cadillac will give Colton Herta another practice outing at the Brazilian Grand Prix to earn him the last point he needs to finally secure his Formula 1 superlicence.

This will be Herta's sixth FP1 outing of the season with Cadillac and he'll replace Sergio Perez. The team only needed to do four to satisfy the rookie practice requirements - but Herta's still short of the 40 superlicence points needed.
That's despite the team initially believing Herta's Mexico FP1 appearance would get him there, which turned out to be wrong because of an error on IndyCar's website .
That error had Herta sixth in the IndyCar standings instead of seventh, creating a miscalculation of two extra superlicence points.
Cadillac did verify that erroneous calculation with the FIA earlier this year but it emerged over the Mexico GP weekend that Herta would need another session to get to 40 points.

Herta picks up one point for finishing 10th in IndyCar in 2023, 30 points for finishing runner-up in 2024, and four points for being seventh in 2025, which, with points for four FP1s (Herta didn't complete enough mileage at Monza to get the superlicence point), leaves him with 39 points currently.
Cadillac was already planning to run Herta in another FP1 session before the end of the year as he's one of the leading contenders to replace Valtteri Bottas in the team next season.
But he can't get that seat if he doesn't have a superlicence, so Cadillac ticking off the last point he needs at the first available opportunity is a logical move.

title: Toyota Innova Crysta Price Hike Nov 2026 Up To Rs 33k
raw_summary: In a move that follows industry trends and is likely due to increased production costs, Toyota has increased prices of its popular MPV, the Innova Crysta. Apart from the equipment list, variants also differ in terms of their seating capacity (7 or 8 seater) and colour options. Platinum White Pearl variants of Innova Crysta command an additional premium in comparison to other colour options. In the latest price hike, the highest increase of Rs 33,000 is applicable on the ZX MT 7S and ZX MT 7S Platinum White Pearl variants.

These numbers should all also apply to the 2027 GMC Sierra , too.

According to documents posted by GM Authority, the fuel economy of all Silverados equipped with either the new 5.7-liter V8 or the new 6.6-liter V8 has dropped between 1 and 2 mpg across city ratings, highway ratings, and combined ratings. While these drops aren't especially significant, it's rare to see redesigned versions of cars debut with worse efficiency than their predecessors, even when we're talking about big trucks.

2027 Silverados fitted with the 5.7-liter V8 are rated at 16 mpg city, 19 mpg highway, and 17 combined in two-wheel-drive form; opting for four-wheel drive drops both the highway and combined ratings by an additional mpg. Those city and combined figures are each down one mpg, and the highway rating is down two mpg compared to the 2026 Silverado.

Trucks with the 6.6-liter V8 are only shown in four-wheel-drive, and are rated at 14 mpg in the city, 18 mpg on the highway, and 15 mpg combined. If you go for the off-road-oriented Silverado ZR2, it drops the city and combined figures by 1 mpg and the highway figure by 3 mpg. (The same should go for the Sierra's AT4X equivalent.) All of those numbers are down by either 1 or 2 mpg when compared to their fuel economy ratings in 2026.

Even opting for the 3.0-liter inline-six turbodiesel powertrain option won't save as much fuel as it did last year. Most diesel-powered 2027 Silverados return between 1 and 2 mpg worse than last year, except for city mileage in some four-wheel-drive trims. City and highway mileage for the diesel ZR2 remains the same. Mileage ratings for the turbocharged 2.7-liter four-cylinder powertrain have not been published yet.

Considering that the Chevrolet Silverado almost always lands in the second-place spot on the list of best-selling vehicles in the U.S. behind the Ford F-Series, and the GMC Sierra isn't too far behind, the impact of small changes in efficiency get magnified. So far through the third quarter of 2026, GMC sold 252,639 Sierras and Chevrolet sold 413,383 Silverados, and production of the new-gen trucks only just started in October. Though not all of these trucks will be fitted with one of the new V8s, certainly a ton of them will, and decreasing even just V8 gas mileage by a single mpg will still result in a massive increase in collective fuel usage.

With a record of more than 300,000 electric vehicles sold last month, BYD sold more EVs than the US did in the entire third quarter, combined.
A big part of the higher demand is thanks to BYD’s latest breakthrough technology, including its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology.

BYD began equipping vehicles with the new battery and charging tech in March, and over the past six months it has posted higher year-over-year sales growth. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 vehicles, up 6% compared to the same period in 2025.
On October 13, BYD launched the Great Han, or “Da Han” in China, the first fully electric D-segment flagship sedan in its Dynasty lineup.
Just 19 days after its launch, BYD said Great Han EV sales reached 4,000 units. At that rate, sales could reach 10,000 or more in its first full month.
With “class-beating high value,” BYD said, “it has firmly established itself in the mid-to-high-end sedan segment above 250,000 yuan,” which is about $37,500.

The Great Han is available in three variants, priced from 235,900 yuan, or about $35,000. Buyers can choose from single- or dual-motor powertrains. The standard rear-wheel-drive (RWD) Premium trim offers up to 1,008 km (626 miles) of CLTC range, while the all-wheel-drive (AWD) Flagship variant offers up to 880 km (546 miles).

article_paragraphs: Nissan's SEMA concept count is up to six, and the topless Armada is, by far, the most extreme

Nissan definitely has its hands full at this year's SEMA Show in Las Vegas. In addition to revealing a special Sentra concept and a pair of exciting Z cars , Nissan has presented a trio of wild off-road concepts based on the Frontier, Pathfinder, and Armada. While the concept cars are ready for some track fun, these concept trucks and SUVs are all about extreme off-roading.

Though these vehicles are concepts, previous SEMA concepts from Nissan have spawned production models, like its current Rock Creek lineup, so Nissan may eventually sell elements of these builds to customers. We don't ever expect to see a topless version of the Armada making its way into production, but could the next-gen Xterra get some off-road accessories like this? We sure hope so.

"As we look toward a future of even more capable trucks and SUVs, including an all-new Xterra, these SEMA Show concepts allow builders to unleash their creativity, while also exploring ideas and innovations that can help inform the direction for accessorizing future Nissan trucks and SUVs," said Kim Less, vice president of Aftersales and Customer Loyalty at Nissan Americas.

Of the three builds, the Frontier Ronin Concept is the one we'd like to see on sale at a Nissan dealership. Its exterior has been transformed with a range of Nismo Off Road accessories, including rock sliders, a roof rack, a spare tire carrier, six-inch driving lights, four-inch A-pillar lights, and prototype flared front and rear fenders. Nissan's team has also crafted high-clearance front and rear bumpers for the Frontier, ensuring that not even the most difficult terrain can stop this truck.

To make sure this Nissan Frontier doesn't just look the part but also performs, the suspension has been overhauled with new Bilstein Black Hawk M 9400 four-way adjustable coilovers with high- and low-speed compression adjustment, plus adjustable rebound and bypass damping. A set of race-spec upper and lower control arms has also been fitted alongside new race spindles, extended axles, and custom rear shock absorber mounts. It also has new 17-inch wheels and a big brake kit.

Like a normal Frontier, the Ronin Concept features the brand's familiar 3.8-liter VQ38DD V6 engine. However, it has a pair of turbochargers from a GT-R Nismo, plus an ECUTEK engine management system and a custom air intake. Regardless of how much power this beast has, it'll almost certainly provide the most fun you can have behind the wheel of a Frontier.

The most extensively modified vehicle of the three is the Jungle Patrol concept. After the Armada Nismo , we didn't think Nissan's full-size SUV could get much wilder, but this concept proves us wrong. The most obvious change is that the SUV's roof has been chopped off and replaced with a black tubular roll cage, giving drivers that open-top off-roading experience perfected by the Jeep Wrangler and Ford Bronco. Complementing the new tubular roof are tubular steel front and rear bumpers, custom fender flares, Nismo Off Road rock sliders, and Nismo Off Road six-inch lights at the front. The Armada's interior has been stripped out and replaced with new bench seats.

title: Mid-Air Helicopter Collision Near Everest Base Camp Kills Tourist, Injures 2 Others
raw_summary: Although an entire tourism industry has grown around climbing Mount Everest, summiting the world's tallest mountain remains a tremendously dangerous endeavor. Two helicopters collided in mid-air while attempting to land at the same spot below the Everest base camp. Helicopter company Fishtail Air stated that the crash killed an Indian tourist, and the chopper's captain and another passenger were injured. The other helicopter's pilot somehow escaped without injury. The second chopper was only carrying cargo. The footage is harrowing, to say the least. A red helicopter is hovering, gradually descending and rotating to a landing spot at Pheriche. The Nepali village sits 13,780 feet above sea level. Then, a second helicopter comes into frame, seemingly appearing out of nowhere. Both pilots take evasive action far too late. The second chopper's main blades smash into the other rotorcraft, slicing off the tail boom. Both helicopters immediately plummet right into the snowy terrain as people waiting on the ground scramble away. Miraculously, none of the bystanders were struck by flying debris or injured. There's never a good outcome when two helicopters hit each other .

The footage is harrowing, to say the least. A red helicopter is hovering, gradually descending and rotating to a landing spot at Pheriche. The Nepali village sits 13,780 feet above sea level. Then, a second helicopter comes into frame, seemingly appearing out of nowhere. Both pilots take evasive action far too late. The second chopper's main blades smash into the other rotorcraft, slicing off the tail boom. Both helicopters immediately plummet right into the snowy terrain as people waiting on the ground scramble away. Miraculously, none of the bystanders were struck by flying debris or injured. There's never a good outcome when two helicopters hit each other .

It's pretty baffling how two helicopters could collide in completely clear conditions. Maybe the pilots didn't realize they were trying to land in the same spot. Helicopter flights aren't rare in this part of the world, either. According to the BBC , helicopters are the only way to get trekkers and guides down from Everest when they are sick or exhausted in inhospitable conditions. It's also the tail end of the mountain's autumn climbing season.

The tourists who spend thousands of dollars to climb Everest do so with the understanding that it's inherently dangerous. Those dangers are typically low oxygen levels and freezing temperatures at absurdly high altitudes. Just getting to the mountain can be just as dangerous. Most journeys to Everest base camp begin at Tenzing-Hillary Airport , named after the first mountaineers to climb the mountain. The facility is often called the world's most dangerous airport because of its short 1,729-foot runway with a 12% gradient and the mountain wall at one end. Not to mention, the terrain doesn't allow pilots to go around despite the rapidly shifting weather conditions. Just flying in would be enough of an Everest adventure for me.

title: Acura Begins Selling 3,000 NSX Restoration Parts In The United States
raw_summary: Why get a new NSX when you can just factory restore the best one? Honda wants to keep as many original NSXs on U.S. roads as possible and has just begun selling more than 3,000 reproduction parts to owners nationwide through the Honda Heritage Parts program . Honda announced the program earlier this year, and it first launched in Japan.
summary: Why get a new NSX when you can just factory restore the best one? Honda wants to keep as many original NSXs on U.S. roads as possible and has just begun selling more than 3,000 reproduction parts to owners nationwide through the Honda Heritage Parts program .
article_paragraphs: Why get a new NSX when you can just factory restore the best one?

Honda wants to keep as many original NSXs on U.S. roads as possible and has just begun selling more than 3,000 reproduction parts to owners nationwide through the Honda Heritage Parts program . Honda announced the program earlier this year, and it first launched in Japan.

Honda's Heritage Parts program includes two categories. The first is Genuine Honda Reproduction Parts, where parts are reproduced using the same methods and materials as the originals, as is the case with the NSX parts. The second is Honda Compatible Parts, which manufactures newly developed parts to replace original ones. The 1991-2005 NSX is the first model Honda is focusing on with its new parts division, and it's expected to grow to include other models in the future.

American owners can purchase reproduced parts from Acura dealerships nationwide and through the Honda DreamShop. A dizzying array of parts is available. So, whether you're completely restoring an NSX in your garage or simply need to service it and replace some aging parts, the Japanese car manufacturer has you covered.

The parts available depend on the specific NSX year, model, trim, and transmission type. For a 1994 NSX with a four-speed automatic transmission, available engine parts include fuel injectors, a new throttle body, exhaust manifold components, an oil cooler, an alternator, clamps, cylinder head covers, camshafts, timing belts, and pretty much anything else you can think of.

The same goes for the automatic and manual transmissions the NSX was sold with. New transmission cases are available, as are gear shafts, bolts, shift forks, and shift levers. Honda also offers reproduced exhaust parts, radiators, electrical connectors, headlights, taillights, and interior gauges. You can also order reproduced wheels, brakes, and shock absorbers. An abundance of interior trimmings and parts can also be ordered online or through an Acura dealership. Chipped your NSX's original windshield? Honda now sells a genuine replacement. Owners can also order easy service items like spark plugs, wiper blades, fuel pumps, and genuine oil filters.

"Honda Heritage Parts was created to help our customers enjoy their classic Acura and Honda performance models, and it's appropriate that we begin with an iconic model like the first-generation Acura NSX," executive vice president at American Honda Motor, Mamadou Diallo, commented. "By supporting our customers in preserving the legacy of the NSX, we're celebrating our shared passion for these iconic sports cars and keeping them on the road for today's enthusiasts and future generations."

It's not just reproduced and new parts that will keep classic NSXs on the roads for years to come. Earlier this year, the Japanese carmaker launched the Honda Restoration Service . It is currently only available in Japan for JDM first-generation NSX models and offers full restoration packages for owners, using the reproduced parts.

Following increasingly strained relations between Ocon and the team, a heated argument in Mexico proved the final straw that made team principal Ayao Komatsu decide to bench the Frenchman. Reserve driver and Toyota protege Ryo Hirakawa replaced Ocon from Saturday onwards in Mexico, going on to score a point on debut in 10th place. The team has now confirmed Ocon, who is a free agent next year, will not return.
"We have now notified Esteban Ocon that he will not return to a race seat with TGR Haas F1 Team this season," Komatsu explained.

"Such decisions are never made lightly, as was the case in Mexico City - but then, as now, we feel this is firmly in the best interest of the team moving forward. The conversations that ultimately unfolded between the team and Esteban remain an internal matter, and we will continue to respect the private nature of closed-door situations."

Ferrari junior Camara, who had already been signed by Haas to replace Ocon for 2027, will take the wheel of the VF-26 at Interlagos. The Brazilian, who currently leads the Formula 2 standings and made a stellar impression on Haas in private testing, will have the opportunity to begin his F1 career several months ahead of schedule.

The final green light came on Tuesday afternoon, although Camara had already been placed on standby during the Mexican Grand Prix weekend following Ocon's sudden removal from the Haas line-up. At the Autodromo Hermanos Rodríguez, the American team fielded Ryo Hirakawa as a temporary replacement while assessing its options for the remaining races of the season.
It is not yet confirmed whether Camara or Hirakawa will race for the team in the remaining rounds at Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi, with it likely being a combination of both drivers.
Rafa Camara has conducted private testing in older machinery with both Ferrari and Haas.

title: These Are the Bestselling Electric Pickup Trucks
raw_summary: Electric pickup trucks are still a relatively new idea, but they've now been along long enough to gather some data on how they're selling. We totaled sales numbers from 2024, 2025, and 2026 so far to see which electric pickup trucks have had the biggest impact on the market in the past few years. For some perspective, electric pickups still make up a tiny portion of the overall truck market in the U.S. Even if you combine the sales of all six models listed here, over a time period of nearly three years, you get 232,809 units sold in total. Ford sold 801,525 units of the F-series pickup in 2025 alone . There are also aren’t any pickup trucks on our list of the bestselling EVs in 2026 , a list which contains mostly SUVs.

article_paragraphs: Electric pickup trucks are still a relatively new idea, but they've now been along long enough to gather some data on how they're selling. We totaled sales numbers from 2024, 2025, and 2026 so far to see which electric pickup trucks have had the biggest impact on the market in the past few years.

For some perspective, electric pickups still make up a tiny portion of the overall truck market in the U.S. Even if you combine the sales of all six models listed here, over a time period of nearly three years, you get 232,809 units sold in total. Ford sold 801,525 units of the F-series pickup in 2025 alone . There are also aren’t any pickup trucks on our list of the bestselling EVs in 2026 , a list which contains mostly SUVs.

The sales totals for each model listed here include figures from the full-year 2024, the full-year 2025, and through the third quarter of 2026. In cases where the automaker doesn't release detailed sales figures, we used estimates from Cox Automotive.

If you feel like you see Cybertrucks everywhere you go, that's not just because their distinctive styling makes them stand out on the road. Tesla has sold quite a few pickup trucks in the past few years, which may seem surprising given the Cybertruck's polarizing design and numerous recalls early in its production run. Tesla started selling the Cybertruck in 2024, and that was the strongest year of sales, suggesting that eager early adopters made up much of the early run of 38,965 units sold that year. Sales declined to around 20,000 units in 2025, and through the third quarter of 2026 Tesla has moved an estimated 11,586 units.

Ford was one of the first to enter the electric-truck market, and its strategy hinged on the F-150 Lightning's similarities to the top-selling F-150 pickup. The F-150 Lightning has since been discontinued, ending production in 2025, but it managed to rack up a significant number of sales. Keep in mind that the Lightning went on sale for the 2022 model year, well before many of the other models on this list, so the sales totals here reflect only the latter half of its production run.

General Motors' Hummer EV pickup was also early to the trend, debuting for the 2022 model year like the F-150 Lightning. But it took a completely different approach with its wild styling, mega-horsepower powertrain, and ridiculous off-road capability. GMC added an SUV sibling for 2024, and the caveat to the Hummer's sales numbers are that they include both body styles. We aren't able to break out numbers for just the pickup, because GM doesn't report those figures separately.

Chevy's electric version of the Silverado pickup got off to a slow start, racking up less than 8000 sales in 2024, its first year on the market. Those numbers picked up for 2025 as Chevrolet added lower-cost variants meant for fleets, cresting 11,000 units that year. But it appears demand has softened once again, as Chevy only moved 5327 units through the first three quarters of this year.

Rivian's debut model was the R1T, which was exactly as innovative as you would expect from a startup automaker. With impressive performance, futuristic styling, and new ideas such as a storage tunnel between the cab and the bed, the R1T aimed more at lifestyle buyers than at traditional pickup customers. The R1T went on sale for the 2022 model year, and sales have been on a steady decline since 2024, Rivian's recently launched compact R2 SUV is now outselling the larger R1 lineup, which makes us wonder if there is room for Rivian to add a pickup version of that model that would offer a lower cost of entry.

title: Pennsylvania is way ahead on NEVI charging - now comes another $37M
raw_summary: Pennsylvania is putting $37 million in federal NEVI funding toward what PennDOT says will be 515 new public EV charging ports across the Philadelphia region, including curbside chargers. The awards cover Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties. PennDOT says the projects will expand public charging availability by 27% across the region and 53% in Philadelphia.

article_paragraphs: Pennsylvania is putting $37 million in federal NEVI funding toward what PennDOT says will be 515 new public EV charging ports across the Philadelphia region, including curbside chargers.
The awards cover Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties. PennDOT says the projects will expand public charging availability by 27% across the region and 53% in Philadelphia.
For drivers without a driveway, curbside charging gives them somewhere to plug in while parked near home.

It’s Electric PA received $2.93 million for 157 on-street Level 2 ports across 13 Philadelphia neighborhoods. Voltpost received funding for another 62 curbside ports across the four suburban counties.

Fast charging is getting funding, too. PositivEnergy received $7.2 million for 54 DC fast-charging ports at 11 Philadelphia Parking Authority lots. Tesla received two $392,000 awards for eight ports each at Royal Farms in Broomall and Wawa in Plymouth Meeting.

The money comes from the federal National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program, created by the Biden administration’s Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Pennsylvania’s five-year allocation is $171.5 million.

NEVI initially focused on fast charging along designated highway corridors. States can spend the money more broadly after the Federal Highway Administration certifies that their corridor charging requirements have been met. Pennsylvania received that certification on September 22, 2025.
In fact, Pennsylvania has built 54 EV charging stations using NEVI funds so far – more than double the number of any other state.

raw_summary: Prepare to say goodbye to Range Rover’s two most affordable models, as the Evoque and Velar celebrate their final model year in production. The Evoque and Velar’s sales have accounted for just 6000 of Land Rover’s U.S. sales through this year. Paltry numbers, representing only 10 percent of the brand’s 2026 sales volume in the U.S. so far. It would not surprise us if North America is not one of the global markets the company considers a high-demand market for these two models. We asked for clarification from JLR but have not heard back.

The two SUVs are attractive not only for their styling but also for their relatively low prices compared with the six-figure ask for the flagship Range Rover SUV. The Evoque starts at around $52,000 and the Velar at around $64,000. Both ride on the same platform as the Land Rover Discovery Sport SUV, which was discontinued after the 2026 model year.

The move comes amid a broader strategy shift at JLR, Jaguar and Land Rover’s parent company. In the past year, both brands have focused on launching electric-powered flagships, the most buzzworthy of which is the Jaguar Type 01 sedan .

Range Rover has launched the Range Rover Electric and is preparing a Range Rover Sport Electric , effectively electrifying its core lineup. A new entry-level Range Rover GT is also on the way and will effectively replace the Evoque and Velar once it hits production as a 2028 model.

Like the Jaguar Type 01, the Range Rover GT takes the shape of a long and low sedan-like vehicle with a minimalist interior and an all-wheel-drive electric powertrain. The Range Rover GT will launch first as an EV, but the company says the platform is capable of hosting gas and hybrid powertrains as well. A starting price of around $90,000 is expected, significantly increasing the entry price to the Range Rover brand.

title: Fat Fender Garage's GT/FX Pairs Sporty Looks with an 800-HP V-8
raw_summary: Ford has produced a diverse array of vehicles in its 123-year history, from workhorses like the bestselling F-series trucks to supercars like the GT supercar . Now, a small outfit seeks to blend the philosophies of those two vehicles. Fat Fender Garage, a restoration shop based in Arizona, has revealed the GT/FX at SEMA, taking the body of a 1956 F-100 truck and giving it performance chops meant to emulate the capabilities of the Ford GT. The GT/FX’s steel body was drastically reshaped by Fat Fender Garage, with a flatter hood and roof and wider front and rear fenders giving it a more aggressive stance. The custom running boards blend neatly into the rear fenders, while a chin splitter up front and a rear diffuser swiped from a Mustang GT350 give the GT/FX a track-ready look.

Now, a small outfit seeks to blend the philosophies of those two vehicles. Fat Fender Garage, a restoration shop based in Arizona, has revealed the GT/FX at SEMA, taking the body of a 1956 F-100 truck and giving it performance chops meant to emulate the capabilities of the Ford GT.

The GT/FX’s steel body was drastically reshaped by Fat Fender Garage, with a flatter hood and roof and wider front and rear fenders giving it a more aggressive stance. The custom running boards blend neatly into the rear fenders, while a chin splitter up front and a rear diffuser swiped from a Mustang GT350 give the GT/FX a track-ready look.

The bed now features distinctive flared edges, and the tailgate drops down with the push of a button. The side-view mirrors are fashioned from carbon fiber, and the gray paint job is completed with a black racing stripe just offset to the left. The only thing left untouched was the grille, maintaining a tie-back to the original F-100.

Behind that grille sits a Gen 3 Ford Coyote 5.0-liter V-8 with a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger strapped on top, pushing out 800 horsepower and 750 pound-feet of torque. The hearty engine is paired with Ford’s 10R80 10-speed automatic transmission, which routes that muscle to HRE wheels wearing Toyo Proxes Sport 2 tires, measuring a beefy 315/35R-20 at the rear. Stopping duties are handled by Wilwood disc brakes with six-piston front calipers and four-piston rear calipers.

The cabin features modern-looking bucket seats; a modern screen and buttons are also part of the transformation, but they’re discreetly integrated. Plus, there’s a concealed climate-control system that blows air through a hidden vent, and there’s also interior LED lighting and a modern audio system.

The GT/FX showcases the breadth of Fat Fender Garage’s abilities, from paint to interior trim and exhaust setups. The truck even rides on the company’s own FF1 Performance Coilover chassis, which is designed to provide sporty handling despite the vintage truck’s body on top. Between the bodywork, the cabin, the powertrain, and the chassis, Fat Fender Garage went all in on transforming the F-100 from a utilitarian hauler into a sport truck that blends classic styling with modern power.

Caleb Miller began blogging about cars at 13 years old, and he realized his dream of writing for a car magazine after graduating from Carnegie Mellon University and joining the Car and Driver team. He loves quirky and obscure autos, aiming to one day own something bizarre like a Nissan S-Cargo, and is an avid motorsports fan.

title: Ford Settles Transit Trail Class Action Lawsuit By Paying Owners Less Than The Package Cost
raw_summary: The current trend of automakers "off-roadifying" their road cars has created a new breed of hiked up, black plastic-clad soft roaders that buyers can't seem to get enough of. Ford gave its Transit full-size van the treatment back in 2022 with the all-wheel-drive Transit Trail, but recalled all of them in early 2024 and replaced their 30.5-inch all-terrain tires that rubbed against the wheel wells with the same 28.5-inch tires on standard Transits, and owners were not pleased. They were so displeased, in fact, that they filed a class action lawsuit that we first reported on last year . Ford finally reached a settlement with the plaintiffs last week, offering Transit Trail owners a $6,000 payout for the diminished off-road abilities of their vans. This is a pretty healthy payout from a class action lawsuit settlement, but it's still less than half of the original price of the Trail package that cost $12,500 when new.

This is a pretty healthy payout from a class action lawsuit settlement, but it's still less than half of the original price of the Trail package that cost $12,500 when new.

According to classaction.org , "Eligible for the settlement are all individuals who, as the original owner or lessee, bought or leased a model year 2023 or 2024 Ford Transit Trail before June 1, 2024 for personal, family or household use and who have not already received any compensation from Ford, including any settlement payment or repurchase, related to a covered vehicle or to any alleged defect of, or economic loss relating to, the vehicle." More fine print about how to prove membership in the settlement class is available on the Class Action site.

The Ford Transit Trail was marketed by Ford as having an "adventure-ready chassis is re-tuned and tested to meet the same BUILT FORD TOUGH durability standards as the rest of the Transit lineup," complete with 6.7-inches of ground clearance, upgraded underbody protection, and the 30.5-inch Goodyear Wrangler Workhorse tires that led to the recall. The 28.5-inch tires that Ford replaced the Wranglers with reduced the ground clearance of Transit Trails down to 5.5-inches, or the same as the standard Transit. Nearly 2,000 vehicles were included in the recall, but it's not immediately clear how many owners are eligible for this class action lawsuit settlement.

Plenty of questions remain after the announcement, including who will drive the entries and what the Gen 7 Charger's bodywork will look like.

The team partnering with Dodge was never a question. Kaulig Racing first paired up with Ram for the brand's return to the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series this season, fielding five Ram trucks. It's surprising how quickly Stellantis North America cobbled together a Cup program. NASCAR confirmed that Dodge completed its wind tunnel testing and will have its production body panels ready later this month. Tim Kuniskis, Stellantis' Head of American Brands, said:

"Everyone said it was impossible to get back in one year. We said, 'watch this,' Sure, we could spend three years planning, testing and perfecting ... or we could do all three in real time, on the track. It's going to be exponentially harder this way. But slow has never been part of Dodge DNA. LFG."

The biggest reason why a Dodge program for the Cup Series was organized in only a year is that the manufacturer will not be building its own engines. Dodge has yet to announce where it will source Kaulig's 2027 motors, but it is in talks with a third party. The Athletic reported that ECR Engines could potentially build engines for Dodge. The partnership has issues because ECR currently produces Chevrolet engines and is owned by Richard Childress, a Chevrolet team owner. NASCAR, Ford and Toyota would need to approve an exemption for ECR to build engines for both Chevy and Dodge.

Besides the powerplant, Kaulig expects to announce its 2027 Cup Series driver lineup this weekend ahead of the season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway. It wouldn't be a shock if the team retained its current pairing of Ty Dillon and A.J. Allmendinger . However, the driver market has seen a major shakeup over the past month. Brad Keselowski is departing RFK Racing, a team he co-owns, after falling out with fellow co-owners Fenway Sports Group. He stated last weekend that he will be available to race elsewhere regardless of manufacturer. Keselowski won Dodge's most recent Cup Series title with Penske in 2012. The 42-year-old admitted that he hasn't discussed anything with Dodge or Kaulig, but he's open to the idea.

raw_summary: " Grand Theft Auto VI " is set to be the biggest video game of the decade, if not one of the biggest games ever made. That distinction isn't just figurative either because it's set to be absolutely huge in the literal, bits and bytes sense, too. Developer Rockstar Games announced Tuesday that the highly anticipated title will be available for digital pre-load starting November 10, and that the full game file will take up to 212 GB, "depending on your device," even telling gamers to "make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible." To put that number into context, the standard PlayStation 5 comes with an advertised 1 TB or 825 GB of storage depending on whether you get the disc or digital version, and about 158 GB of that is taken up by the operating system. In other words, assuming the standard PS5 version of the game is indeed 212 GB and you've got a digital console without any external drives, just GTA VI will take up more than 25% of all your available space.

In other words, assuming the standard PS5 version of the game is indeed 212 GB and you've got a digital console without any external drives, just GTA VI will take up more than 25% of all your available space.

On the Xbox side, a Series X comes with either 1 TB or 2 TB while the entry-level Series S is offered in 1 TB or 512 GB drives, and of course, a good chunk of that is always reserved for the OS. Big thoughts and prayers for owners of the 512-gig Series S.

Given how much content this next Grand Theft Auto game is set to come with, a massive download isn't entirely surprising. The map is said to be double that of "GTA V," three times bigger than "Red Dead Redemption 2," and will apparently include "hundreds" of accessible building interiors. There are also hundreds of cars to account for , super detailed character models, and, y'know, the underlying logic and systems that make it all a playable game.

All that said, it's entirely possible that the quoted 212 GB size is only for the higher-fidelity PS5 Pro version of the game, and that console comes with 2 TB out of the box. However, the fact that Rockstar is quoting that number only as a blanket sort of thing leads us to believe that the standard version most people will download is indeed just as big, or not meaningfully far off.

Grand Theft Auto VI will release (or, for those who pre-load, become playable) on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S consoles. For the real keeners, pre-load starts on November 10 — midnight local time on PS5, midnight GMT for Xbox.

raw_summary: The Luce, Ferrari’s first electric car and one of its most polarizing models, isn’t just selling. It’s selling out. article_paragraphs: The Luce, Ferrari’s first electric car and one of its most polarizing models, isn’t just selling. It’s selling out.

The five-seater EV designed by Jony Ive, Apple’s longtime design chief, was mocked and widely panned when it debuted in May, sending Ferrari’s stock price lower. But all that criticism hasn’t dampened demand, according to CEO Benedetto Vigna.

The 2027 production run of the Luce, which starts at about $615,000, is “fully allocated,” Vigna said Tuesday during the company’s third-quarter earnings call, meaning every car Ferrari plans to build next year already has a buyer. “If someone comes, he has to wait one year to get the cars,” Vigna added. The first deliveries of the Luce are expected to begin in the fourth quarter.

Just how many Luce cars that represents is unclear. Ferrari has never publicly disclosed how many Luce vehicles it plans to produce. Financial Times reported earlier this year, citing unnamed sources, that Ferrari planned to sell just under 500 units this year. The company’s longer-term target is to sell 2,500 units by 2030, or about 600 a year, according to Financial Times.

Speculation on who these buyers are — ahem, the founders of multibillion-dollar AI labs, perhaps? — will have to remain just that until Luces are spotted in the wild. Vigna wouldn’t provide a breakdown of who these Luce customers are, only noting it was a “good mix in terms of client, it is a good mix also in terms of geography.” He later added that there is no specific pattern or demographic of Luce buyers.

While Luce deliveries have yet to begin, Ferrari’s existing lineup and growing demand for personalized options helped fuel its financial performance in the third quarter . Revenue from customizations, which executives said accounted for more than 21% of revenue from cars and spare parts, helped boost profits. The company said deliveries of the F80, its limited-run hypercar , and customization reflect its clients’ “ever-deepening desire” to make each Ferrari uniquely their own. As a result, the company raised its full-year guidance, saying it now expects adjusted earnings of at least €3 billion ($3.36 billion), up from €2.97 billion.

Ferrari, which enjoys some of the highest profit margins in the auto industry, reported third-quarter revenue of €1.9 billion, up 7% from a year earlier, and net income of €431 million, up 13%. Operating profit was €563 million, for an operating margin of 29.7%, meaning the company kept roughly 30 cents of every dollar of revenue as profit from its core business.

article_paragraphs: Jeep has just done something with the Wrangler that has never been done before: given it independent front suspension, and somehow, that's not even the wildest part of its latest concept vehicle. The automaker just pulled the covers off the Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept at the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, and right away you can tell this thing is no ordinary Jeep truck.

Right above that independent front suspension sits a naturally aspirated 6.4-liter HEMI V8 with 470 horsepower and 470 pound-feet of torque on tap. Out back, you'll find a Trophy Truck-style rear axle. The whole truck is finished in what Jeep calls Punk'n orange, and its bed is actually pretty functional while also serving as a nod to Jeep's own Scrambler history . It has reversible jump seats that let rear occupants face either forward or backward toward the rear of the truck — a layout built for desert chase trucks and spotters. Is it a gimmick? Yeah, but it's also sick as hell.

Equally sick as hell are the looks — especially up front where designers clearly took inspiration from the CJ-8 Scrambler of the early 1980s. However, it's a damn slight more aggressive than that car with its shark nose front end and massively flared fenders. The rear, while much shorter than your typical Jeep Gladiator, looks fairly similar. The body itself is far shorter as well, which isn't surprising when you consider it only has two doors. All in all, it doesn't look too dissimilar from the Jeep Sandstorm Concept we saw back in 2018 , but they're certainly different vehicles.

Since the dawn of man, Wranglers have had solid front axles, but that changes for the Scrambler SRT. Developed with off-road racer Casey Currie, the new independent front suspension delivers 14 inches of travel up front and 15 inches out back. Jeep says the goal is better high-speed stability, more precise steering (impossible for it to be less precise) and better wheel control when blasting through the desert. This is a Jeep aimed at desert running, not the rock-crawling crowd that usually flocks to Wranglers.

As I mentioned earlier, the Trophy Truck-inspired rear suspension is its own feat of engineering. It's built to soak up high-speed impacts rather than slowly articulate over rocks. When paired with beefy 37-inch tires, it's clear that the Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept is designed for off-road speed first and foremost. While I do love rockcrawling, there's nothing quite like prerunning to really get the heart pounding.

Of course, none of this is really, well, real. The Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept is very much a concept, though I'll admit, I won't be too shocked if the Wrangler ends up getting independent front suspension at some point in the future. The Ford Bronco has it, and the Earth has yet to collapse in on itself despite that.

While this concept is still unmistakably a Jeep, Tim Kuniskis , head of American Brands, SRT Performance and Direct Connections at Stellantis North America, said the project was a dare to the brand's own playbook, which is probably where the use of an IFS comes in. Sure, it's going to tick some Jeep loyalists off, but some departures are good departures.

Its immediate opportunity includes replacing diesel backup equipment at data centres, where exhaust, noise and permitting can be genuine obstacles. The company also describes a larger market for firm power at grid-constrained sites, including systems operating around the clock. The electrochemistry is established, but delivering competitive electricity requires a materials supply chain that the generator specifications do not describe. An aluminum–air cell consumes aluminum. It does not accept electricity through a charging cable and return to its original chemical state. Aluminum reacts with oxygen and water, producing electrical energy and aluminum hydroxide, sometimes called aluminum trihydrate. The generator needs more metal when the fuel is spent, and the hydroxide has to be collected, transported and either sold into another market or processed further. The aluminum brought to a data centre already embodies substantial electricity used earlier to turn aluminum compounds into metal. That upstream energy belongs in the assessment.

Its immediate opportunity includes replacing diesel backup equipment at data centres, where exhaust, noise and permitting can be genuine obstacles.
article_paragraphs: California startup Voya Energy announced a $35 million financing round in August 2026 for generators that use prepared scrap aluminum, air and water to produce electricity without combustion. Its immediate opportunity includes replacing diesel backup equipment at data centres, where exhaust, noise and permitting can be genuine obstacles. The company also describes a larger market for firm power at grid-constrained sites, including systems operating around the clock. The electrochemistry is established, but delivering competitive electricity requires a materials supply chain that the generator specifications do not describe.

An aluminum–air cell consumes aluminum. It does not accept electricity through a charging cable and return to its original chemical state. Aluminum reacts with oxygen and water, producing electrical energy and aluminum hydroxide, sometimes called aluminum trihydrate. The generator needs more metal when the fuel is spent, and the hydroxide has to be collected, transported and either sold into another market or processed further. The aluminum brought to a data centre already embodies substantial electricity used earlier to turn aluminum compounds into metal. That upstream energy belongs in the assessment.

I encountered the same supply-chain issues when I examined Wright Electric’s aluminum–air aircraft proposal in 2021 . Prepared aluminum would have needed delivery to airports, followed by collection and processing of spent material. Data centres avoid the aircraft weight constraint, while retaining the need for deliveries of prepared fuel and industrial handling of reaction products.

The operating schedule determines the size of that problem. Voya’s August announcement emphasizes diesel replacement while also describing larger, continuously available power installations. To test the larger proposition, I calculated the materials needed for a hypothetical 100 MW data centre supplied continuously by aluminum–air generation. Using the company’s reported 57% conversion efficiency and aluminum’s theoretical electrochemical energy, the system consumes roughly 520 metric tons of metal each day and produces about 1,500 metric tons of aluminum hydroxide. That becomes approximately 190,000 tons of incoming metal and 550,000 tons of outgoing material each year. The additional byproduct mass comes from oxygen and water incorporated in the reaction. These are scenario quantities, not measured operations at a Voya site.

An intermittent backup generator could consume orders of magnitude less aluminum annually than the continuous 100 MW case, changing the economics of deliveries and residue handling. Voya’s interest in low-grade contaminated scrap deserves examination, since some metal streams are difficult to sort into high-quality recycled products. Yet scrap is not automatically valueless because it is contaminated. Recycling aluminum into new metallic products uses approximately 95% less energy than making primary metal, and improving scrap recovery is itself an important industrial decarbonization opportunity. Buying that scrap as expendable fuel can compete with other recovery routes as their technology and economics improve.

Voya initially expects to sell aluminum hydroxide and proposes metal regeneration as a longer-term option. Those are different uses for the spent material. A 2026 lifecycle assessment modeled electricity-to-electricity round-trip efficiency of 29–35% for aluminum–air storage pathways involving regeneration. That finding is not a test result for Voya’s equipment, but it indicates how much additional electricity and processing could be needed to close the material loop. A company selling the hydroxide cannot also assume it will recover that same material for fuel without buying it back.

Voya’s published metal-price target leaves limited room for other costs. In a 2025 California Energy Commission submission, the company listed targets below $0.30/kWh for delivered electricity and $0.50 per pound for the metal fuel. At 57% conversion efficiency, the latter implies about $0.24/kWh for aluminum alone, before fuel preparation, generator capital, transport, residue handling or financing. Saleable hydroxide could provide an offset where purity, processing costs and buyers support it. The generation target remains a target, rather than a demonstrated commercial tariff.

There may be worthwhile applications for compact, noncombustion backup power where diesel is hard to permit and suitable scrap is readily available. Continuous power for large AI facilities calls for a much larger comparison with grid connections, generation and rechargeable batteries. The chemistry works, but the economics must account for every load of metal delivered, every load of residue removed and the electricity consumed upstream.

Its immediate opportunity includes replacing diesel backup equipment at data centres, where exhaust, noise and permitting can be genuine obstacles.
