raw_title: Tesla cuts FSD’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in Europe
title: Tesla cuts FSD's speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in Europe
raw_summary: Tesla’s driver-assistance system in Europe can no longer be set to drive 50% over the speed limit. The Netherlands’ RDW, which approved the system in April, confirmed today that it signed off on an update capping the speed margin at 10% and officially renaming “FSD Supervised” to Tesla Assisted Driving. The changes land weeks before EU member states could vote on approving the system across the bloc, and they match the conditions Germany set last month.
summary: Tesla’s driver-assistance system in Europe can no longer be set to drive 50% over the speed limit. The Netherlands’ RDW, which approved the system in April, confirmed today that it signed off on an update capping the speed margin at 10% and officially renaming “FSD Supervised” to Tesla Assisted Driving.
article_paragraphs: Tesla’s driver-assistance system in Europe can no longer be set to drive 50% over the speed limit. The Netherlands’ RDW, which approved the system in April, confirmed today that it signed off on an update capping the speed margin at 10% and officially renaming “FSD Supervised” to Tesla Assisted Driving.
The changes land weeks before EU member states could vote on approving the system across the bloc, and they match the conditions Germany set last month.

The RDW’s notice is the clearest official confirmation of how the system was configured when the Dutch regulator approved FSD Supervised on April 10 . The “speed margin,” which lets the system deviate from the detected limit for “safety and traffic flow,” could go up to +50%. On a 100 km/h highway, that’s 150 km/h. In a 30 km/h city zone, it’s 45 km/h.
Now the margin tops out at +10%. It also resets to 0% every time the car starts, and the RDW says other speed-related functions are now disabled by default. It didn’t say which ones.
The new name shows up on the in-car display, in the owner’s manual, and in other driver information on HW4 vehicles. Tesla pushes all of it over the air.

The RDW describes the update as “several minor changes” that Tesla asked it to assess. The regulator says it checked the implementation, found no adverse or unintended effects, and folded the changes into the existing type approval without amending or extending it. It also stresses that the rename doesn’t change what the system does. It’s still driver assistance, and the driver is still responsible.

The RDW notified the nine member states that recognize its approval: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. That’s 10 countries counting the Netherlands, up from eight at the start of October.

The EU-wide decision still sits with the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV). The RDW says those talks are confidential and won’t comment on them. As we reported, the EU pushed the vote to December at the earliest , and passing it takes a qualified majority: 15 of 27 member states representing at least 65% of the EU population.

title: Why Bearman is yet to be announced as a Haas driver for F1 2027
raw_summary: With Oliver Bearman firing on all cylinders in his sophomore Formula 1 campaign, it feels odd that Haas has been able to confirm the identity of Esteban Ocon's replacement in the second seat for 2027 before announcing Bearman is staying put for a third year. There is no real doubt that Bearman will stay where he is, with both parties keen to continue for another season into 2027.
summary: With Oliver Bearman firing on all cylinders in his sophomore Formula 1 campaign, it feels odd that Haas has been able to confirm the identity of Esteban Ocon's replacement in the second seat for 2027 before announcing Bearman is staying put for a third year.
article_paragraphs: With Oliver Bearman firing on all cylinders in his sophomore Formula 1 campaign, it feels odd that Haas has been able to confirm the identity of Esteban Ocon's replacement in the second seat for 2027 before announcing Bearman is staying put for a third year.
There is no real doubt that Bearman will stay where he is, with both parties keen to continue for another season into 2027.

“I think it's very clear. I want to continue with Haas and that's definitely my goal," Bearman said in Mexico on Thursday. "It's not really in my hands. If it was up to me, it would have already been announced a long time ago, but there are a few bigger picture things that we're working on."

Team principal Komatsu added: "I don't like to go into the details of our contract, but Ollie is showing amazing potential. He's contributing a lot to the team's success and we want to grow together. We want to move up the grid as a team.”

And while Komatsu had to dismiss unsubstantiated rumours over Bearman's pay demands, holding up a deal as "absolute nonsense", the real reason behind the delay is not about 2027, but about what happens next.

Autosport understands that should Ferrari be unable to guarantee him a seat in 2028 - after three years of being loaned out to customer team Haas - then Bearman will have the freedom to part ways with Maranello. It is this "bigger picture" that Bearman was referring to in his answer, and a picture that has become increasingly clouded in recent months.

Bearman is still on course to complete the full Ferrari Driver Academy pathway, all the way from F4 to a race seat with the Scuderia - Charles Leclerc being the only driver thus far to have completed the entire trajectory.

But a new road block has emerged in the shape of Lewis Hamilton, who has regained form this year and exercised the contractual option that secured his place at Ferrari for 2027. While Bearman initially looked like a perfect successor to Hamilton, the seven-time world champion's recent comments in the media about his longevity do not portray a man who is walking away from Ferrari and F1 anytime soon. Leclerc, meanwhile, has already agreed a long-term contract extension until at least 2030.

One of these cities is Plymouth, Minnesota, where Joel Feder of The Drive was wrongfully accused of driving a stolen car based on a bad Flock hit. The city council voted to cancel its contract with Flock on September 22, and officially notified Flock the following day. From The Drive :

[Plymouth Police Chief Eric] Fadden said, "We did not hear any reply from Flock Safety Corporate or Legal, other than some communication with our local representative." Flock's silence and refusal to comply with the canceled contract forced the Police Chief to take matters into his own hands. "After hearing nothing for more than a week, I directed our staff to disconnect the power cords from the cameras in order to be sure that they are not functioning or recording plates," Fadden said.

It's rather ironic that the chief of police ended up instructing his officers to do exactly the same thing some vandals have done to disable the cameras. With Flock not responding to multiple attempts to cancel the service, this appeared to be the only way to be sure the cameras were off, as the city council's vote required.
Other cities have taken this process a step further, removing the cameras and storing them until Flock wants them back. From KARE 11 :

"Once we made this decision, I personally went to the locations and removed the cameras and poles myself," Crystal police chief Pete Underthun told KARE 11 in a statement. "We are still working with the company to close out our contract and for them to pick the cameras up from our garage."

I guess what would otherwise qualify as vandalism is fine if the police do it themselves. Dayton, Minnesota, also physically removed its cameras, but even that didn't shut down the service. As the city explained in a Facebook post :

On September 17, 2026, the Police Department was made aware of a maintenance work order produced by Flock. The City notified Flock on September 18, 2026, that the program was on hold, and no work orders were to be completed. Unfortunately, the City's direction was not followed, and the camera was placed back into service without authorization. Following the report, City staff reviewed locations throughout the community to determine whether any additional cameras had been reinstalled, and one additional location was identified. article_paragraphs: Sauber isn't a strange way to say Saab, also a defunct auto brand . Nor is it in any way related to the Sauber racing team that finally closed shop in 2025, giving way for Audi to take a seat at the Formula 1 table . The Sauber we are talking about today was an extremely short-lived Austrian car brand that existed from 1993-1995, solely to import American cars to Austria to sell them under the Sauber name. Well, it was a little more complicated than that. Its relative obscurity sent YouTuber corsicar on one of the most amusing missions of discovering what exactly the brand was, and more importantly, "why?"

Prior to corsicar's deep dive into this mysterious car company, knowledge on Sauber had been little to none. It seemed to have made it into the curious car chasm in 2025 via TheTruthAboutCars , and an Autopost article done shortly after. One simply cannot internet search Google themselves into a hole for hours taking in information on Sauber otherwise. Coriscar, however, found a newspaper ad for a vehicle called a Sauber Villager. It looks strangely similar to Mercury's Villager. Almost identical, because it is the same vehicle. This gets the whole search rolling.

The Sauber brand was established by a married couple in Austria in 1993. After getting things situated in Austria, the owners founded another company in the U.S., in Florida, Sauber Automobiles USA, Inc. This was likely to get around import laws and accruing unwanted taxes .

According to a review Coriscar found of the Sauber Villager in Auto Revue magazine , the Florida office was used to purchase American vehicles that would then be registered in the U.S. From there, it could export those vehicles to Austria, where they'd get a light facelift to make changes to meet Austrian regulations, and with a little rebadging, they'd officially be "Sauber" cars, as demonstrated by the ads found and shared in the video.

The company essentially tried to make a complete lineup of in-demand or soon-to-be in-demand vehicles using different American market models. There was the family hauler, minivan or MPV Sauber Villager, which was the Mercury Villager, a Ford product, which was also a Nissan product. Sauber's mid-size sedan, coupe and or wagon, the Messager, was General Motors' Saturn S-class sedan, 2-door coupe, and wagon. The entry-level econo-car was the unfortunately named Sauber Teenager, or a Ford Aspire. And the sporty car was the Sauber S1, which was a Dodge Stealth or Mitsubishi 3000GT.

Sauber models went on sale in 1994 with 12 existing dealers. The hope was to expand to 30 by mid-year. At those dealers, interested buyers could consider the cheaper, poorly named Teenager at around $14,500 (in 1994), the Messager at $22,000, the base Villager at $41,600, its top-of-the-line First Class trim level cost around $54,700, and the S1 offered at $76,100. Just for kicks, to give you an idea of how much that costs today with inflation, the Teenager would start at $33,000 and the top of the line, sporty S1 would be just shy of $175,000.

To get the attention of potential buyers, Sauber really played with the Austrian sense of humor. One ad shown in the video reads (in Austrian) "In life you have to try everything at least once. A test drive in a Sauber doesn't hurt either." Pictured below the text was a Sauber Villager (or basically edited Mercury Villager), and above the text, a pair of boxing gloves, cigars, and a leather crotch harness for you know exactly what.

It seems the ads were not funny enough because in May 1995 documents show the Commercial Court of Vienna rejected the car company's intent to declare bankruptcy, and instead officially declared the company dissolved. Sauber was so broke, it had nothing to help pay off debtors in a bankruptcy. What ruined it isn't clear. Importing cars from another country is an expensive endeavor. Buying a car to then make costly adjustments to them to meet regulations likely didn't help either. The whole model doesn't feel very viable. It also happens that a new tax introduced in 1994 — the Austrian Value-Added Tax Act — would have subjected those imports to heavier taxation.

article_paragraphs: This 1,000-hp beast will be parked at SEMA in the FuelTech booth

The McLaren MP4/1 of the 1981 F1 season was the first car to use carbon fiber extensively in its construction, and it wasn't until 1990 that the Jaguar XJR-15 became the first road-legal car made entirely from carbon, including the chassis and bodywork. The world now has an all-carbon-fiber-clad 1967 Ford Mustang Shelby GT500 courtesy of Classic Recreations, bringing a modern material to a car that predates its automotive use by more than a decade. Yet, there's more to this GT500 than carbon fiber.

Unveiled at SEMA, this is one of the first cars Classic Recreations has built since Velocity Restorations took over last year. Dubbed the Shelby GT500CR , it is the only carbon-fiber Mustang of its kind officially licensed by Shelby. The carbon looks absolutely astonishing, covering every exterior panel and contrasted with red-tinted carbon fiber racing stripes.

Classic Recreations has built several carbon fiber-clad Ford Mustangs before, with several selling for in excess of $500,000 . The company unexpectedly filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy last July , citing between $1,001,000 and $10 million in outstanding liabilities. Florida-based restomod builder Velocity Restorations acquired and saved it last November and locked in a new licensing deal with Shelby to keep building these cars. While we sometimes get bored of the dizzying array of restomods hitting the market, we'll never get tired of seeing classic Mustangs fitted with modern powertrains like this.

For as impressive as the carbon fiber skin is, this Mustang's engine is the real headline. It's driven by a modified Coyote 5.0-liter V8 with a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger and a standalone FuelTech GT700 ECU. The V8 is rated at a monstrous 1,000 horsepower and drives the rear wheels through a 9-inch Ford rear end, a carbon fiber driveshaft, and a 10-speed automatic transmission. A traction control system has been added, giving it a chance to put the power to the ground.

The modifications don't stop with the new bodywork and engine. The car includes new front and rear suspension systems, Nitron electronically controlled shocks, and a stainless-steel fuel tank. It sits on bespoke Forgeline wheels with Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires and also includes a stainless exhaust. Perhaps the most interesting and surprising upgrade is on the braking front. Positioned at both the front and rear are 14.9-inch (380 mm) carbon-ceramic discs, working alongside six-piston front calipers and four-piston rear calipers. This should give the car more than enough braking performance to match the 1,000 hp brute of an engine.

The car's interior has also been tweaked. It includes a Vintage Air air conditioning system, a Dakota Digital cluster, new floor mats, custom seats, and an Ididit steering column. Some carbon fiber has been added to the transmission tunnel for that extra exotic feel, and a new Alpine head unit has been included. If the owner wants to listen to their favorite tunes, new Focal K2 speakers have been fitted alongside a Mosconi amplifier. However, if we had to pick between listening to music or enjoying the supercharged V8 to its fullest, it'd be that raging Coyote.

raw_summary: A base Ford Bronco makes 300 horsepower. Opt for the V-6 option, and it’ll add 30 horses; if that’s not enough, the Bronco Raptor reaches 418. Not there yet? Try doubling the Raptor’s output and adding a few hundred more horsepower. Enter the Megazilla 2.0. Ford’s most powerful crate engine ever is now on display for the first time at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Megazilla 2.0, which builds off the 7.3-liter V-8 crate engine lineup, uses a stronger block, upgraded pistons, larger fuel injectors, a different belt drive and damper, and a supercharger-specific camshaft to keep up with a 3.0-liter Gen 6 Whipple supercharger. All of that combines to make over 1200 horsepower and over 1000 pound-feet of torque.

Ford’s most powerful crate engine ever is now on display for the first time at this year’s SEMA show in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Megazilla 2.0, which builds off the 7.3-liter V-8 crate engine lineup, uses a stronger block, upgraded pistons, larger fuel injectors, a different belt drive and damper, and a supercharger-specific camshaft to keep up with a 3.0-liter Gen 6 Whipple supercharger. All of that combines to make over 1200 horsepower and over 1000 pound-feet of torque.

To show off the engine’s massive output, Ford developed the Frostwarden: a search-and-rescue-inspired Bronco taken to extremes. The outfitted Bronco is lifted with a 74Weld portal lift kit and wears 42-inch-tall BFGoodrich tires mounted on custom 18-inch Weld beadlock wheels. Dana driveline hardware and custom Bilstein dampers round out the undercarriage upgrades.

The Frostwarden’s black-and-yellow livery, ultra-wide stance, and plethora of rescue tools—including off-road lights, a rear-mounted external gas tank, roof-mounted spare tire, and bright yellow front tow winch—make the Bronco hard to miss, even among the ranks of modded SEMA show cars. Inside, yellow-and-black upholstery lines the cabin and a special Megazilla wordmark rests along the bottom of the steering wheel.

The Frostwarden is a one-of-a-kind build, but the 7.3-liter supercharged V-8 that powers it isn’t. Ford says the one-off vehicle highlights the ability to launch extreme builds based around Ford-powered engines, including the massive Megazilla 2.0.

Alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck."

title: Rivian spinout Also was working on an e-moto project in Kenya
raw_summary: Also, the micromobility startup spun out of Rivian in 2025, quietly started and then walked away from an electric two-wheeler pilot project in Kenya earlier this year, as it sought to focus its resources on its consumer e-bike and autonomous vehicle ambitions, TechCrunch has learned. The project received grant funding from the Shell Foundation, an independent charity established by the British oil and gas giant Shell plc. A section of the Shell Foundation’s website that has since been removed said the project’s goal was to “enable and de-risk global OEM entry into Africa’s EV market by piloting a locally integrated electric two-wheeler platform in Kenya, with potential to scale across East Africa.”
summary: Also, the micromobility startup spun out of Rivian in 2025, quietly started and then walked away from an electric two-wheeler pilot project in Kenya earlier this year, as it sought to focus its resources on its consumer e-bike and autonomous vehicle ambitions, TechCrunch has learned.
article_paragraphs: Also, the micromobility startup spun out of Rivian in 2025, quietly started and then walked away from an electric two-wheeler pilot project in Kenya earlier this year, as it sought to focus its resources on its consumer e-bike and autonomous vehicle ambitions, TechCrunch has learned.

The project received grant funding from the Shell Foundation, an independent charity established by the British oil and gas giant Shell plc. A section of the Shell Foundation’s website that has since been removed said the project’s goal was to “enable and de-risk global OEM entry into Africa’s EV market by piloting a locally integrated electric two-wheeler platform in Kenya, with potential to scale across East Africa.”
According to the deleted section, Also was expected to work on modular battery designs, distributed EV charging, and planned on “developing a purpose-built electric motorcycle for African riders.”

The opportunity for electric motorcycles seems ripe on the continent, which has a massive two-wheeler market. African mobility company Spiro recently said it has more than 130,000 electric motorcycles operating across seven countries, along with 2,500 battery-swapping stations. This boom has drawn interest from Chinese mobility companies and investors, which are pouring resources into the space .

In a September email, Also told TechCrunch that it had “explored this project” with an unnamed partner, but ultimately “decided to focus on its core roadmap” after completing only “some early-stage work.” Also said the grant funding it received from the Shell Foundation “will follow the project to support its ongoing development,” but declined to offer specifics.

The Shell Foundation told TechCrunch in an email that the project was “intended to generate evidence on driver income uplift potential, operational performance and commercial viability to deepen the company’s understanding of the market opportunity.” But when TechCrunch asked for more specifics, the Shell Foundation declined, citing a nondisclosure agreement with Also. Days later, the project disappeared from the Shell Foundation’s website.

During an interview last month at TechCrunch Disrupt, Also co-founder and president Chris Yu said the Kenya pilot project initially made sense given Also’s mission to build small, purpose-built vehicles that are “first and foremost cost-optimized to do the job that needs to be done in a particular market.”
But other projects took precedence, Yu said, especially the development of small autonomous vehicles — which Also is working on as part of a partnership with DoorDash .

title: McLaren to bring upgrades to Brazil GP with F1 2027 in mind
raw_summary: McLaren will introduce upgrades to its MCL40 Formula 1 car at this weekend’s Brazil Grand Prix, featuring a front wing concept which is expected to feature on its 2027 challenger. The team had surged to the front when it substantially updated the MCL40 in Hungary, with Lando Norris winning that race and the following one at Zandvoort, but it has since slipped back in the pecking order despite introducing another comprehensive upgrade package in Baku and further new parts in Austin.
summary: McLaren will introduce upgrades to its MCL40 Formula 1 car at this weekend’s Brazil Grand Prix, featuring a front wing concept which is expected to feature on its 2027 challenger.
article_paragraphs: McLaren will introduce upgrades to its MCL40 Formula 1 car at this weekend’s Brazil Grand Prix, featuring a front wing concept which is expected to feature on its 2027 challenger.

The team had surged to the front when it substantially updated the MCL40 in Hungary, with Lando Norris winning that race and the following one at Zandvoort, but it has since slipped back in the pecking order despite introducing another comprehensive upgrade package in Baku and further new parts in Austin.

McLaren had the fourth-quickest car in the last four qualifying sessions, with a 0.511s deficit to pole position and a 0.236s gap to the third-fastest challenger on average, but is still working away at improving the MCL40 – with an eye on 2027.

“We’ve got some updates coming to the car across the front wing, rear wing and some floor components as part of our normal development cycle,” said Peter Prodromou, chief technical officer, aerodynamics. “The aim is to make up ground, improve our performance over the remaining races and build momentum into next year.
“Sao Paulo has been a good circuit for us in the past and is a fairly representative track, so we’re hopeful these upgrades can help us take another step towards the front.

“The season isn't over yet: these upgrades are designed to improve the car now and help us in our fight for third in the championship. While the learning we take from these upgrades will feed into next year’s development, we also expect to carry over the concept of the new front wing into the launch specification of next year’s car.”
McLaren has a 17-point deficit to third-placed Red Bull but has scored just 59 points to its rival’s 152 across the last five rounds.
The Mexican race was still encouraging, with Norris taking fifth just 12 seconds adrift of race winner Max Verstappen , yet the reigning world champion wasn’t optimistic for the next few rounds.

But the engine's essentially the same three-cylinder that's found in a Mini, and there's no manual, so they can't be that expensive.

The cheapest BMW i8 I could find with a clean title is listed for $33,299, or what those of us in the business call "the danger zone." That's juuuust cheap enough that a normal person could convince themselves it's a good idea to buy a depreciated luxury car, only to get hit with huge bills. Obviously, a normal person should never buy a heavily depreciated, low-volume German car that's incredibly complicated and already more than a decade old. Me, though? I think I might replace my Fiat 500e with an i8 when the lease is up.

Obviously, since the Fiat is a coupe, and I'm never having kids, it makes sense that I'd replace one coupe with another, but you're probably assuming I want the BMW i8 because it's a gorgeous mid-engine sports car that I can buy at an affordable price. That's incorrect. You see, I actually want the beautiful BMW with the carbon-fiber chassis because I'm a good person who cares about the environment. Yes, it offers great balance and agile handling in a comfortable, daily drivable package that looks like an exotic, but I need you to believe I only want the BMW i8 so I can help save the planet.

You can buy all sorts of cars for about $33,000, but as far as practical rides go, it's hard to beat the Honda Civic Sport Touring Hybrid . It's comfortable, offers pretty much all the bells and whistles, and its hybrid powertrain is rated at 49 mpg combined. That's the kind of good, responsible car you buy, and oh, isn't it nice it also has 200 horsepower and 232 pound-feet of torque? A hybrid Civic is the car someone my age probably should buy, but I just care about not giving kids asthma too much to get the reasonable Honda.

Remember, the BMW i8 is a hybrid, too. In fact, it's a plug-in hybrid. And because of that, despite making enough power for Car and Driver to hit 60 mph in 4.0 seconds flat , it's also incredibly fuel efficient. Keep that battery topped off, and it's rated at 76 MPGe, which is more than 49 mpg. The i8 also has 15 miles of electric-only while the Civic has none. You see, I can't buy the Honda because I can't afford to. I need the BMW and its sweet billionaire doors because it's so much more efficient.

Could you imagine driving a car that got less than 50 mpg? I certainly couldn't. I need to get at least 75 mpg to feel good about all the tire particles my car feeds the salmon , and the only car I can think of that meets my needs is the BMW i8. So if you really think about it, the two-door German and its laser headlights is just the more practical choice. That's not a slight at the Civic, either. I'm sure it's a very nice car if you like modern features and refinement. It's just not the car I need because it's not the BMW i8. And I need the BMW i8 because I care about saving the planet. You believe me, right? I need you to promise you believe me here.

title: Dixon set to replace Mir in Qatar MotoGP round
raw_summary: Former Moto2 and current World Superbike racer Jake Dixon is set to get his first Honda MotoGP start at this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, according to The Race's sources in the paddock. Dixon, who recorded two MotoGP starts back in 2021, is to slot into the factory Honda team amid Joan Mir's ongoing illness.

article_paragraphs: Former Moto2 and current World Superbike racer Jake Dixon is set to get his first Honda MotoGP start at this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, according to The Race's sources in the paddock.
Dixon, who recorded two MotoGP starts back in 2021, is to slot into the factory Honda team amid Joan Mir's ongoing illness.

A World Superbike rider from 2026 onwards, the 30-year-old Dixon has had an injury-ravaged first campaign there - missing the first five rounds of the championship thanks to a pre-season wrist injury. He was believed to have originally joined the Superbike team with an option to step into a MotoGP replacement rider role if needed.
Instead, it was his team-mate Somkiat Chantra who got that chance, replacing Mir at the Japanese Grand Prix last month and matching his career-best MotoGP finish of 13th on an improving RC213V.

Mir was forced to withdraw before the halfway point of last weekend's Malaysian Grand Prix due to a recurrence of the eyesight problem that had also left him fatigued. He had previously skipped four straight rounds.

"We already knew with the doctors that if I was having some dizzy moments due to the heat and due to these difficult conditions, I would stop," he explained after his Sepang DNF. "And I started to get a bit dizzy on lap nine.
"I was not having control of the situation and I decided to stop. We will continue working and hopefully we will sort the situation as soon as possible.
"Honestly, I worked so much to try to be in a better situation. All the weekend, I think it was a positive weekend.

raw_title: Toyota Confirms the Celica’s Return as a Rally Race Car for 2027
title: Toyota Confirms the Celica's Return as a Rally Race Car for 2027
raw_summary: The Toyota Celica is coming back, and it’s going racing. Toyota today revealed its plans for the 2027 World Rally Championship, and the automaker decided to compete with two separate teams running two different cars. While Toyota Gazoo Racing will run the GR Yaris, a new team simply called Toyota Racing will field a new GR Celica rally car, which is expected to eventually spawn a road-going version too. Both cars will compete in the top Rally1 class. The GR Celica race car will ride on a new control chassis that will be shared among all teams competing in Rally1 as part of a regulatory change for 2027. The new rules will also see Rally1 cars use adapted versions of the turbocharged 1.6-liter inline-four engines currently found in the Rally2 class. This means the GR Yaris Rally1 and GR Celica Rally1 will essentially be identical underneath, differentiated only by the bodywork placed atop the chassis.

While the GR Celica will start its racing career in 2027, we may have to wait quite a bit longer before we can get behind the wheel of a new Celica on public roads. Changes to the rules mean that WRC teams can now race with cars that do not have a road-going counterpart, although we still expect Toyota to build a new Celica production car. The common chassis and engine in Rally1 next year allowed Toyota to pull up development of the race car, but the road car is still years away and will have little in common with the race car under the skin.

Rumors have pointed to a mid-engine platform that Toyota is working on, also expected to underpin a return of the MR2 sports car , although this platform could also be exclusive to the MR2. Other reports have suggested a front-engine setup for the GR Celica, which would be more in line with the Celica’s heritage. The GR Celica Rally1 car will mount its engine up front.

Earlier this year, the head of Gazoo Racing, Tomoya Takahashi, said the mid-engine platform had only entered the first of four development stages, and the platform isn’t expected to be ready until closer to 2030. The platform is also expected to usher in a new turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four, codenamed G20E, that could push out north of 400 horsepower.

Even if the Celica doesn’t use this mid-engine platform, it could still be a few years away, since minimal information about the production development has slipped out of Toyota’s walls. A previous report suggested it may even be an all-wheel-drive hybrid, but no powertrain details have been confirmed.

title: The Homeschooled Crowd Just Figured Out Lunch Tray Drifting
raw_summary: Evidently, and yes, I'm dating myself, lunch tray drifting has been out of the curriculum for a bit. Proof that you don't need a custom, 750-horsepower Dodge Charger drift car to have some parking lot fun, a group of friends just discovered that putting plastic under the rear tires of a front-wheel-drive car makes it considerably more willing to slide. Their discovery of this fact is documented on TikTok , and it's about as wholesome and entertaining as any car-related content can be these days. Rather than lunch trays, the video starts with a guy positioning plastic cutting boards under the rear tires of what looks like a Ford Focus ST . If that's the correct model — and the exhaust routing indicates that it is — it's already a potent little car. But the one big thing about it, and all other FWD or FWD-biased hot hatches, is that they are missing a majority of power to the rear wheels.

article_paragraphs: Evidently, and yes, I'm dating myself, lunch tray drifting has been out of the curriculum for a bit. Proof that you don't need a custom, 750-horsepower Dodge Charger drift car to have some parking lot fun, a group of friends just discovered that putting plastic under the rear tires of a front-wheel-drive car makes it considerably more willing to slide. Their discovery of this fact is documented on TikTok , and it's about as wholesome and entertaining as any car-related content can be these days.

Rather than lunch trays, the video starts with a guy positioning plastic cutting boards under the rear tires of what looks like a Ford Focus ST . If that's the correct model — and the exhaust routing indicates that it is — it's already a potent little car. But the one big thing about it, and all other FWD or FWD-biased hot hatches, is that they are missing a majority of power to the rear wheels.

Behind the camera, his friend has already reached a verdict: "There's no way this is gonna work." "It's gonna work," the driver replies. He closes the door. His friend doubles down: "It's not gonna work." You can probably guess what happens next.

The car pulls away, its rear end sliding every which way as the cameraman's certainty dissolves into laughter. "No way. No shot... no shot," he says. Someone sure has a few old parking-lot drift videos to catch up on. The comments provide the history lesson. "Aww to be young. We definitely used McDs trays 20 years ago," one reads. Another gets straight to the point: "People rediscovering tray sliding."

It may not look as cool as a rear-drive drift car spewing smoke from the back tires, but placing some thick, flat plastic under the unpowered rear tires of a front-drive car reduces grip and allows the back end to slide. For those who might have tried this in the past and struggled, engaging the parking brake will often keep the back tires from moving while the fronts do whatever you tell them to. Suddenly, just about any FWD commuter can be an enthusiastic, DIY drifter.

That said, it's worth considering a few things before you try this. First, some modern cars will keep you from accelerating if they sense that the parking brake is on. Second, the plastic in question can wear out quickly. Third, there's no telling how some modern systems will react to the rear wheels being stationary while the fronts spin and steer normally. In the end, though, this can be a great way for folks to learn car control, so they don't make a fool of themselves by destroying a Pagani Zonda HP Barchetta or wrecking a Bugatti Chiron . Just be sure to drive safely and pay for the cutting boards you use. Stealing them from the lunch lady or McDonald's isn't very nice.

Kuniskis said that while everyone they’ve spoken to has told the company they’ll need a minimum of three years to develop their Cup car, the company doesn’t want to wait that long. Instead, Dodge is planning to return to the series from the onset of the 2027 season—where it’ll be forced to adapt and develop their car and program in real time.

title: The Jaguar Type 01's U.S.-Spec Bumper Is Fantastically Well Integrated
raw_summary: We may be long past the days of requiring extraordinarily ugly impact bumpers be affixed to cars sold in the U.S., with those laws extending to supercars like the Lamborghini Countach , cars that are driving around on American roads still aren't quite as smooth as they may be in other markets. Whether for insurance reasons like the Bugatti Chiron or to meet regulatory crash safety regulations, U.S.-spec versions of some cars (typically wild-looking, high-end ones) sometimes get bumpers that protrude slightly further out, or have bumperettes or bumper guards added on. The latest victim of this is the Jaguar Type 01 , except its little U.S.-spec bumperette solution is actually extremely well done, perfectly integrated with its outrageous styling. I got to see the Type 01 in person for the first time at the Las Vegas Concours over the weekend, and I love it even more in the metal than I already did in photos. Luckily our American-market modifications haven't ruined that.

The latest victim of this is the Jaguar Type 01 , except its little U.S.-spec bumperette solution is actually extremely well done, perfectly integrated with its outrageous styling. I got to see the Type 01 in person for the first time at the Las Vegas Concours over the weekend, and I love it even more in the metal than I already did in photos. Luckily our American-market modifications haven't ruined that.

At the bottom of the body-color strakes in the upright rear end, the Type 01 has a black bar stretching across the same width that houses the parking sensors, with the license plate holder sitting just below it along with a fang-like diffuser design. On the U.S.-spec Type 01, that black bar juts outward a little more dramatically, with angled sections at the ends instead of it being flat all the way across. The rest of the rear end design is exactly the same, and the protruding bumper flows so perfectly with the car's design, you probably wouldn't even notice it if the two cars were side by side.

There is one other difference between Euro- and U.S.-spec Type 01s you may have noticed. Here in America our cars need to have side marker lights and reflectors at front and the rear; usually automakers will integrated these as subtly as possible, maybe along the curve of the wheel arches, following the design of the bumper, or even putting them within the headlights and taillights themselves. Jaguar, though, decided to make them a more prominent part of the car's design.

The Type 01's side markers are squares, positioned low down in the corners of the front and rear bumpers where their lines are aligned with other lines of the car. Yeah, they stand out, and some people will find them to be an eyesore, but I actually like this placement. At least nothing else about the Type 01's lighting design had to be changed for the U.S. market — the headlight arrays are still ultra-thin, and the pair of full-width taillights are still hidden between those strakes.

Other than those two little details, the Type 01's design is identical across markets, which is a good thing. Love it or hate it, you've got to respect Jaguar really swinging for the fences here and creating production car with pure concept-y looks , like it traveled back in time to show off how wild cars will look in the future.

According to the U.S. Constitution, Election Day is to be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November. That means today, November 3rd, 2026, Americans are heading to the polls to vote for stuff and things. This election is being closely watched worldwide, as it's an indication of how the American people feel about President Trump's tariffs, the war of choice with Iran, and immigration enforcement policies. This midterm election is also expected to be influenced by the price of gasoline, just as the price of eggs was a contributing factor in 2024.

These high prices aren't a recent occurrence, either. Recently, the U.S. set a new record for the most days above $4 per gallon , and that recorded hasn't ended yet. As Americans head to the polls today, gasoline costs more than on any Election Day in the country's history. According to GasBuddy , the national average for a gallon of 87 octane gasoline is $4.12. Perhaps a more concerning trend is that the country continues to drain the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which is at its lowest level since October 1982.

Some of you will certainly say in the comments, "If you want to see high gas prices, you should move to Europe." Yes, if you break down the raw cost per ounce of fuel, it is more expensive in other parts of the world, but that doesn't mean the dramatic increase in fuel costs doesn't affect the economy as much as it does elsewhere. Higher fuel prices hurt nearly everyone except oil companies, as those costs pass through to every part of life.

The most jarring aspect of hitting these new milestones is that this week's record coincides with the SEMA Show in Las Vegas. While gas is at a record high, Jeep showed off a "concept" that will likely have a Hellcat V8 as an optional engine. People will certainly buy this Jeep when it goes into production, but in some ways, it feels a bit out of place. No different than GM launching a new 8.3-liter Duramax when the price of diesel fuel is even more astronomical than gasoline — sitting at $6.28 a gallon today.

title: GM's Hybrid Onslaught Will Start With Its Big SUVs
raw_summary: After overcommitting to electric vehicles, General Motors is now developing several new hybrid models to meet growing demand for fuel-efficient vehicles for those not yet ready to commit to an EV. Among the first of these new hybrid models are expected to be hybridized versions of the Buick Enclave, GMC Acadia, and Chevrolet Traverse . GM boss Mary Barra confirmed during the automaker's most recent earnings call that it will build hybrid vehicles at the Lansing Delta Township plant in Michigan. She did not specify which of the brand's existing models will get hybrid powertrains, though sources tell Reuters it will be the three-row Traverse, Enclave, and Acadia models, all of which are already built at the Lansing site. During the earnings call, Barra noted that hybrids will be available across multiple segments, so only the company's big SUVs won't get hybrid options.

article_paragraphs: After overcommitting to electric vehicles, General Motors is now developing several new hybrid models to meet growing demand for fuel-efficient vehicles for those not yet ready to commit to an EV. Among the first of these new hybrid models are expected to be hybridized versions of the Buick Enclave, GMC Acadia, and Chevrolet Traverse .

GM boss Mary Barra confirmed during the automaker's most recent earnings call that it will build hybrid vehicles at the Lansing Delta Township plant in Michigan. She did not specify which of the brand's existing models will get hybrid powertrains, though sources tell Reuters it will be the three-row Traverse, Enclave, and Acadia models, all of which are already built at the Lansing site. During the earnings call, Barra noted that hybrids will be available across multiple segments, so only the company's big SUVs won't get hybrid options.

The only hybrids that GM currently builds are the right-hand-drive Corvette E-Ray, along with the new Corvette Grand Sport X and ZR1X. GM is investing $1.25 billion in the Lansing site to support the upgrades needed to accommodate hybrid models.

Technical details about GM's forthcoming hybrid models are limited. It is believed to be working on both traditional series hybrids and plug-in hybrids. A report from early October suggested that the first plug-in hybrid models are scheduled to launch either next year or in early 2028. These models could offer solid all-electric driving ranges of up to 70 miles (113 km), and the Chevrolet Equinox and Silverado are among those expected to include PHEV options.

General Motors largely ignored hybrids over the past decade and instead aimed to shift from its combustion-dominated line-up to a full suite of electric vehicles. This plan seemed logical until President Donald Trump returned to the Oval Office and scrapped the federal EV tax credit. This triggered a collapse in demand for EVs across the United States, and solely committing to them was no longer a viable choice for GM. Earlier this year , Barra said GM is "trying to be very thoughtful about what we do from a hybrid and a plug-in hybrid perspective," and added that the company's ultimate "end game" remains EVs.

With this in mind, it continues to invest heavily in EVs. Whereas Ford took a $19.5 billion write-down late last year after axing several of its EV projects, GM expects to take a smaller $7.6 billion charge for its reduced EV spending. Earlier this year, GM sold the 49.99% stake it had in a joint venture plant with Samsung SDI due to declining EV demand. This month, GM previewed its fourth-generation EV platform that will underpin several new EVs. The car manufacturer is also developing advanced new lithium-manganese-rich (LMR) batteries that will offer 33% greater energy density than current LFP batteries, all while costing roughly the same.

But that’s far from the only news coming out of Zero’s booth in Milan.

The electric motorcycle maker is also announcing a new street-legal version of its XE electric dirt bike that was previously only street-legal in Europe, introducing its LS3 electric scooter to Europe, introducing a redesigned smartphone app, and sharing more details about its upcoming DC fast-charging system.
There’s quite a bit to unpack here, so let’s get into it.
Perhaps the most exciting announcement is Project Ventura, a new lightweight electric motorcycle that Zero hopes will attract an entirely new generation of riders.

With supermoto-inspired styling, 17-inch wheels, and a more approachable design than the company’s larger street motorcycles, Ventura appears aimed squarely at riders who want something more substantial than a typical lightweight e-moto but aren’t necessarily looking for a full-size, high-performance motorcycle.
And with a targeted price of less than US $8,000, it could be one of Zero’s most accessible street motorcycles yet.
The bike features a new electric powertrain producing over 20 kW (27 hp) of peak power, delivering a sustained top speed of 65 mph (105 km/h) and a momentary maximum speed of 81 mph (130 km/h).

I wanted to know what car you'd definitely lease but would never buy . What car would you happily have in your driveway for two or three years, racking up repair and deprecation costs on the automaker's dime , all just to give it back in 36 months? Of course, you can't get attached to these vehicles, because your time with them is going to be finite, so the emotional folks among us may not like the idea of leasing, and neither will those of us who like to keep cars for years and years.

Of course, you can't get attached to these vehicles, because your time with them is going to be finite, so the emotional folks among us may not like the idea of leasing, and neither will those of us who like to keep cars for years and years.

In any case, why don't you drop on down below and check out what cars your fellow Jalops would consider leasing but would never buy? Did you buy one of the cars on this list? What's it like feeling like a fool in front of everyone?

Oh! Really quick, to everyone who took the time to say they'd never lease a car : shame on you. That wasn't the question, and I don't care. That's why I made a shame slide for the rest of us — folks who are willing to participate in polite society — to gawk at you all. Boo, you!

Anything German. Under lease, I'm protected by free repairs when inevitably something breaks. My pockets aren't deep enough to keep the car running post warranty expiration if it were a purchase or I bought out the lease.

I have this irrational love of the Land Rover Defender. Can't explain why. At least it can be treated like the Land Rover safari vehicles of not long ago. But there is a zero chance I'd ever hang onto one for more than five years, so it's a lease. Insert Land Rover quality stereotype here, but the list of electrical gremlins they suffer is legion. And they don't improve with age. But for that three year lease, I'd beat the snot out of it and buff out any scratches from trees and shrubs at turn-in time.
Land Rover Defender. Why? because not reliable and expensive to maintain. But for the fun and the driving experience.
Alfa Romeo Quadrafoglio. Great looking, hear it's fun to drive. But it's an Alfa...

There are dozens of reasons for and against leasing, but sometimes there are cars that you really just should never, ever buy.

The Alliance for Automotive Innovation , a group representing some of the biggest automakers in the world, including General Motors, Toyota, Hyundai, Ford, Stellantis and Volkswagen, said it was backing the Trump administration in a legal challenge to its sharply lower vehicle fuel economy standards that had been filed by California, New York and two dozen other states, cities and counties around the country. I'll tell ya what, I'm not surprised, but I'm sure those automakers will be once those fuel economy rollbacks are changed in the next administration (whenever that comes).

Last month, the U.S. Department of Transportation said it was finalizing a fleet-wide fuel economy average of 34.9 mpg by 2031. That's down from the 50.4 mpg mark that was set by the Biden administration in 2024 . The group argued that automakers require "certainty and stability" in standards. From Reuters :

It added that if the standards were set aside, it "would affect automakers' ​business, endangering the capital investment planning, product development, and performance validation for hundreds of ​new vehicle models intended for the US market."

The states said the Trump administration was ignoring the presence ‌of millions ⁠of electric vehicles, "leading to a flawed, dramatically distorted analysis of the 'maximum feasible' fuel economy level." The automaker group said the court should reject those arguments.

The revised Trump administration standards seek to reverse Biden's push toward greater fuel efficiency and electric vehicles. A coalition of environmental ​and consumer groups ​also filed a separate ⁠lawsuit challenging the new rules.
The Transportation Department said the regulation reduces manufacturers' average cost per vehicle to comply by $1,289 but increases fuel ​costs by more than $1,600 over the life of the vehicles.

article_paragraphs: I finally got to see the new Tesla Model YL, Model Y Standard, and Model 3 Standard in person a few weeks ago and wanted to give my thoughts on the three models. I drove the two Model Ys and just looked at the Model 3 Standard. I was visiting relatives in Colorado and visited the Tesla dealer in Superior, Colorado (a very progressive part of Colorado). The dealer was very busy, but not quite as busy as I saw when the tax credit was expiring last year.

As I mentioned in this article 4 months ago , I’ve been a fan of the Model YL since it was announced in China, and finally in the US recently. As a parent of 3 kids and an owner of a series of 3 minivans over 30 years, I’m well aware of the criticism that Tesla doesn’t make a car suitable for large families. The Model X was a partial solution to this problem, but had two large flaws in my opinion.

So, I wanted to see if the Model YL solved these two issues with the Model X. The short is answer is that it solved the price issue but not the space issue. The premium launch edition at $61,990, with about $11,000 in free options, is plenty affordable — although, still a bit more than a minivan or a Grand Highlander. In fact, I optioned up a Model Y Premium with similar features (including the 3rd row) and it came out to about $60,000! So, this suggests the Model YL will be available for about $53,000 or approximately a $3,000 upcharge once they stop selling the Launch Edition (similar to the price difference in other global markets). On space, the Model YL is pretty similar to the Model X. Good enough for many families, but not as spacious as minivans, the Grand Highlander, or the Chevy Tahoe. You can see from the screenshot below that the Model YL is sold out for 2026, and the dealer was telling people to not expect them until March 2027.
I thought it would look more different than the regular Y. I found it difficult to tell the difference at a glance.
The second row was very comfortable, with heated and cooled seat and plenty of room and adjustable headrests. A significant upgrade to the second row of the regular Y!

The third row was a mixed bag. The seats are heated, but not cooled. It does have vents for both air conditioning and heat. It’s not as spacious as the first and second rows, but at 6′ 2″, I was comfortable and would be fine on a long drive. I did find it challenging to get to the 3rd row, since the second row didn’t slide forward like it does in many vehicles (including the regular Model Y). You are expected to sneak between the two seats in the second row, which works for most people, but older folks like me don’t like it.

Leg room was adequate (not not generous), but I was more comfortable putting one leg in the middle as shown. Had I moved up the second row, I would have had plenty of room, but then it would have been crowded. I was setting all three rows as best I could for 6-feet-tall people in all 3 rows. This is MUCH better than the 3rd row in the regular Model Y, which is only appropriate for children and small adults.

I was amazed I had an inch or two of space above my head in the 3rd row. I forgot to take any pictures of the first row. It does have an extra thigh support adjustment that is nice, but is mostly just like all of the other Model Y (great, but nothing new). Handling and accelerations were about the same as a Premium Model Y dual motor. The ride was a little softer (the YL has electronically controlled dampers, tuned for comfort) than the 2026 Model Y Premium (frequency dependent passive controlled dampers, tuned for a balance of comfort and handling) and much improved over my 2021 Model Y (conventional passive shock absorbers, great for handling but gives a harsh ride) and the 2026 Model Y Standard (retuned conventional passive shock absorbers, a balance between handling and ride). Full Self Driving (Supervised) was promoted by the sales advisor and was perfect on the short test drive.

raw_summary: The adorable little Eli ZERO electric microcar is growing up. article_paragraphs: The adorable little Eli ZERO electric microcar is growing up. At this year’s EICMA motorcycle show in Milan, Eli Electric Vehicles is unveiling a faster, more powerful version of its pint-sized electric car, along with a sporty new limited-edition model that even includes a hidden Turbo mode.

First teased last week , the new Eli ZERO MX is the company’s first L7e-class electric vehicle, allowing it to reach speeds of up to 80 km/h (50 mph). That’s a significant jump from the 45 km/h (28 mph) top speed of the original L6e version that we originally reviewed , opening the door to a much wider range of driving scenarios.
And perhaps most importantly, the company managed to squeeze that extra performance into the same tiny package.
The Eli ZERO MX retains the original’s ultra-compact 2.25-meter (7.4-foot) length, making it considerably smaller than even the smallest conventional passenger cars.
But under that tiny exterior, the MX now packs up to 20 kW (27 hp) of peak power, compared to the 12 kW (16 hp) of the original Eli ZERO.
The upgraded model also features a 14.4 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery, providing a claimed range of up to 200 km (124 miles) per charge.
That’s a pretty respectable figure for a vehicle designed primarily for short urban and suburban trips.

The rear-wheel-drive microcar features selectable ECO and SPORT driving modes, a 30% climbing capability, and a tight 7.2-meter turning circle. Charging is handled by a 3.3 kW onboard charger, allowing owners to plug in at home or use public AC charging stations.

raw_summary: Toyota has presented a heavily modified version of the bZ electric crossover , designed to serve as an autonomous driving taxi for Waymo. article_paragraphs: Toyota has presented a heavily modified version of the bZ electric crossover , designed to serve as an autonomous driving taxi for Waymo. Operation of the driverless fleet will start in 2027 in Japan, followed by the UK and other Waymo-serviced markets in the coming years. Furthermore, Toyota continues to explore the implementation of Waymo-sourced technology on future models.

The collaboration between Toyota and Waymo was originally announced last year , but the companies have now shared more information about their plans. The highlight is the special version of the Japanese-spec facelifted Toyota bZ4X, which is sold as the bZ in North America.

The EV is fitted with multiple Waymo sensors mounted on the roof, front bumper, front fenders, rear bumper, tailgate, and rear spoiler. The rest of the bodywork is carried over from the standard bZ4X, with a plain white shade and Waymo lettering on the doors.
Besides the exterior hardware, the ride-hailing bZs will also undergo interior modifications. Toyota added automatic doors, a power liftgate, and ambient lighting, while promising ample rear legroom.

Existing Waymo vehicles typically undergo sensor and computer integration after rolling off standard factory floors. However, Toyota will assemble the new bZ robotaxi and install Waymo's Level 4 autonomous hardware in its Takaoka plant in Japan.

The automaker didn't get into details about the specifications of the autonomous EV. The production model rides on the e-TNGA architecture and is available with single and dual electric motors producing up to 214 hp (160 kW / 217 PS). The 74.7 kWh lithium-ion battery pack is good for a WLTP range of up to 314 miles (505 km), although the EPA figure is 252 miles (406 km).

We will learn more about the EV when it starts rolling out in Japan next year. It remains to be seen if the Toyota robotaxis will reach US states like Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Atlanta, potentially replacing Waymo's custom Jaguar I-Pace SUVs that have been around since 2018.

Finally, the companies confirmed they are actively researching ways to incorporate Waymo's self-driving tech into personally owned Toyota vehicles, while teaming up with Toyota's software arm, Woven by Toyota, to leverage real-world operational data with the goal of improving road safety.

Kia sold 80,008 vehicles in the US last month, up 16% year over year and marking its best October sales month ever.
Kia said electrified and hybrid vehicles drove the growth, with sales up 112% and 114% YOY, both setting new sales records.

Several Kia models posted strong YOY sales growth, including the three-row electric EV9 (+111%), Telluride (+63%), EV6 (+58%), Seltos (+43%), Sorento (+31%), Carnival (+17%), K4 (+14%), and Sportage (+12%).
Regarding its fully electric vehicles. Sales of the EV9, Kia’s three-row electric SUV, are now up 5% year-to-date, with 13,835 units sold through October.

We've been pushing vehicles to their limits since 1956 to provide objective data to bolster our subjective impressions (you can see how we test here ). When the Hyundai Ioniq 5 N arrived on the scene back in 2023, it introduced simulated shifting to electric vehicles. We were so enthralled by its combustion-engine cosplay that it played a major part in the 5 N being named our 2024 EV of the Year . But this time, it doesn’t come at a performance cost.

article_paragraphs: Welcome to Car and Driver' s Testing Hub , where we zoom in on the test numbers. We've been pushing vehicles to their limits since 1956 to provide objective data to bolster our subjective impressions (you can see how we test here ).

When the Hyundai Ioniq 5 N arrived on the scene back in 2023, it introduced simulated shifting to electric vehicles. We were so enthralled by its combustion-engine cosplay that it played a major part in the 5 N being named our 2024 EV of the Year . As fun as it is to bang through gears in a vehicle without an engine, our testing proved that the 5 N’s acceleration times significantly suffered in “N e-Shift” mode compared with its standard drive mode. Like the Ioniq 5 N, the new Genesis GV60 Magma—the luxury brand’s first entry in its performance-focused Magma sub-brand—features a “Virtual Gear Shift” mode that mimics the sensations of an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic paired to an internal-combustion engine. But this time, it doesn’t come at a performance cost.
See all results for new 2027 Genesis GV60 Magma for sale near 94112

Beneath the surface, the Ioniq 5 N and the GV60 Magma feature nearly identical hardware. Both are built on Hyundai Motor Group's E-GMP electric vehicle platform, feature a dual-motor all-wheel drive powertrain that produces up to 641 horsepower, make use of an 84-kWh battery pack, and both roll on 275/35R-21 Pirelli P Zero Elect tires, although the Magma gets newer PZ5-spec rubber versus the Ioniq 5 N’s PZ4 Pirellis. Besides the GV60 Magma’s nearly four-inch-shorter wheelbase and 91-pound-heavier curb weight, the differences between the pair are primarily software-related or matters of styling and design.

Some of those discrepancies are superficial—the 5 N’s faux-engine soundtrack mimics a 7750-rpm inline-four while the Magma’s aural signature is based on a 9000-rpm V-6, for example—but others have an impact on performance. Both models can only access their max power output with a time-limited Boost mode, and while the Hyundai can maintain its 641-hp peak in 10-second bursts, the Genesis can continue at full tilt in 15-second increments. That longer duration of peak output allows the Magma to walk away from the 5 N as they approach their Vmax—for example, the Genesis beats the Hyundai to 150 mph by almost two seconds—but otherwise the two were bumper-to-bumper up to 120 mph. The real delta between the Hyundai and Genesis’s straight-line capabilities only surfaces once both are switched into their simulated-shift drive modes.
See all results for new 2027 Genesis GV60 Magma for sale near 94112

The last time we had an Ioniq 5 N at our test track , we performed two separate acceleration runs, once without N e-Shift and once with it activated. Importantly, N e-Shift mode disables the 5 N’s N Grin Boost and launch-control features, essentially robbing it of 40 horsepower and an optimized start, so we conducted the first run without launch control to even the playing field a bit. Still, the 5 N proved to be significantly quicker when it wasn’t hammering through make-believe gears, silently rocketing to 60 mph in 3.1 seconds, reaching 100 mph in 7.2 seconds, and crossing the quarter-mile marker in 11.3 seconds. With N e-Shift activated, it took the Ioniq 5 N 3.5 seconds to reach 60 mph (a four-tenth increase), 8.3 seconds to hit 100 mph (a whopping 1.1 seconds slower than in its standard drive mode), and 11.8 seconds to clear the quarter-mile (five-tenths behind our non-N e-Shift run).

When we conducted the same experiment in the GV60 Magma, we got very different results. During our testing, the Magma achieved nearly identical acceleration figures regardless of its drive mode. In both of its runs, the Genesis managed a 3.0-second sprint to 60 mph, a 6.8-second dash to 100 mph, and a quarter-mile time of 11.0 seconds. (The 0.1-second difference between our reported quarter-mile time of 11.1 seconds for the Magma and the 11.0-second figure quoted here is that, in this case, we were comparing two runs in the same direction, while all of our official acceleration figures are an average of a run in each direction.)

title: Fat Fender's 800 HP Ford F-100 Is The Work Of Over 15,000 Hours
raw_summary: Pickup trucks have changed a lot since the Ford F-100 in 1953, and now come with more space, more practicality, loads of new technology, and much more power. In developing and building a wild 1956 F-100 for this week's SEMA Show, Fat Fender Garage could have taken the project in several different directions. It could have stuck true to the original F-100 and restored it, or perhaps restored one and subtly modified it. Instead, the Arizonan firm has built an F-100 aimed at matching the performance of a modern Ford GT. Put simply, it's extreme.

The wild F-100 , known as the GT/FX, is built around an all-new chassis and uses a 5.0-liter Coyote V8. This is no ordinary Coyote , as it's topped with a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger, delivering a combined 800 horsepower and 750 pound-feet of torque. The engine also features a bespoke Borla exhaust system and pairs with a 10-speed automatic transmission that drives the rear wheels.

Fat Fender Garage says designing and building this F-100 took more than 15,000 hours, and much of that time went into the chassis and suspension. The pickup rides on FF1 performance coilovers that apparently help it "deliver handling akin to a modern supercar." We're doubtful of that claim, although it should certainly handle better than an original F-100 and most modern pickups. Complementing all the added horsepower and torque are large Wilwood brakes with six-piston calipers at the front and four-piston calipers at the rear.

Every piece of the F-100's exterior is new. It features hand-crafted steel body panels, including flared front and rear wheel arches, and a bespoke grille with modernized headlights and air intakes. The coilovers have dropped the Ford's ride height significantly, though Fat Fender Garage has found enough room to fit custom HRE wheels with wide Toyo Proxes Sport 2 tires.

The F-100 also rocks the same rear diffuser as a Ford Mustang GT350 and includes a bespoke chin splitter, running boards, and custom stainless bumpers. The paint is also unique, combining a beautiful shade of silver with black running stripes running over the length of the truck. It looks so good that if we were the proud owner, we might have a little trepidation about driving this beast out on the open road.

There's also no mistaking this F-100's interior from any regular one. It has new leather details, bucket seats, and a modern climate control system hidden within the dashboard. Fat Fender Garage has also equipped it with new gauges, door actuators, and a proper audio system. There's no word on how powerful the audio system is, but it'll have to be strong if it wants to overpower the Coyote V8.

"GT/FX illustrates just how far we can take a classic truck," Fat Fender Garage founder Jason Noel said. "We wanted to bring the attitude of a Ford GT to a '56 F-100 and carry that idea through every aspect of the build. This truck represents the culmination of everything our team has learned and built over the years. From the chassis and interior to the performance systems, fabrication, paint, and final assembly, GT/FX brings the entire Fat Fender Garage ecosystem together in one vehicle."

title: Tesla wins trade zone status for Texas Megapacks, but China tariffs stay
raw_summary: Tesla’s Megapack factory in Brookshire, Texas, is now officially a foreign-trade zone, a US customs program that lets manufacturers defer duties on imported parts. summary: Tesla’s Megapack factory in Brookshire, Texas, is now officially a foreign-trade zone, a US customs program that lets manufacturers defer duties on imported parts. The FTZ Board’s approval, published in the Federal Register on Monday, runs for 14 months. It’s easy to read this as Tesla getting a pass on tariffs for the Chinese LFP cells inside its Megapacks.
article_paragraphs: Tesla’s Megapack factory in Brookshire, Texas, is now officially a foreign-trade zone, a US customs program that lets manufacturers defer duties on imported parts. The FTZ Board’s approval, published in the Federal Register on Monday, runs for 14 months.

It’s easy to read this as Tesla getting a pass on tariffs for the Chinese LFP cells inside its Megapacks. Tesla’s own application says otherwise: parts hit by Section 301, 232, or 122 tariffs still pay them.

Tesla filed the request on May 20 for Subzone 84AM, part of FTZ 84 in the Houston area. That’s the factory where Tesla started Megapack 3 production in August , with a planned capacity of 50 GWh per year.

The application lists roughly 80 imported components Tesla wants to bring in under zone procedures, from coolant pumps and transformers to busbars, wiring harnesses, circuit boards and battery cells. Duty rates on those parts go up to 6.5%, while finished Megapacks and Bento inverters range from duty-free to 3.4%.
That gap is the usual reason companies set up an FTZ. A manufacturer in a zone can normally elect to pay the finished product’s lower rate instead of the rate on each imported part.

But the application spells out the limit. Components subject to duties under Section 122 of the Trade Act, Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act, or Section 301 “require subject merchandise to be admitted to FTZs in privileged foreign status,” according to the notice.

Privileged foreign status locks in a part’s own classification and tariff treatment when it enters the zone. So a Chinese LFP cell that ends up in a Megapack sold in the US still pays the Section 301 tariff on Chinese non-EV lithium-ion batteries, which jumped from 7.5% to 25% on January 1, 2026. Tesla just pays it later, when the finished Megapack leaves the zone.
The approval came with the same wording the FTZ Board has used all year. Production was “authorized on a limited basis,” and “further subject to a fourteen-month time period.”

Hey, maybe Trump knows something about algae biofuel…

The Reflecting Pool is a massive body of shallow water that extends from the foot of the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, DC. Situated on filled ground in former marshlands, the Reflecting Pool provides a golden opportunity to showcase the ability of the domestic biofuel industry to take advantage of the built infrastructure, rather than taking up valuable farmland with conventional energy crops like corn or soybeans.

Although algae cultivation was probably not the original intention of the Reflecting Pool, it has been a perennial host to algae ever since its construction in the 1920’s, with the humid environment and temperate climate of DC lending a hand.

In earlier years, the Pool was drained and refilled twice a year to control the growth. By the 1990’s, the structure was clearly sinking into the marshes, sparking calls for a major structural overhaul and the addition of a water circulating system .

The soup-to-nuts rehab was completed in 2012, and yet the algae persisted. Finally, when Trump took office for the second time in January of 2025, he lit upon a brilliant idea of turning lemons into lemonade. The Reflecting Pool would be re-made as a monument to the domestic algae biofuel industry.

By the summer of 2026, the transformation was complete and the algae were thriving , as confirmed by satellite imagery. Others mocked, but the President stood by the plan. After all, biomass is a key element in his “American Energy Dominance” policy , and where better to showcase biofuel than in the nation’s capitol, to be seen and admired by millions of tourists.

And so, that explains why Trump chose the Reflecting Pool as the seemingly incongruous scene of his Election Day eve closing message, as reported somewhat incredulously by The Guardian among many others.

“On the eve of a consequential election day, with polls indicating that most voters feel the US president has grown too focused on building projects in the nation’s capital, he stood in front of the newly opened reflecting pool to discuss – in detail – changes to the pool’s pipe, the grass surrounding the area and granite,” observed The Guardian .

The modern reinterpretation of the CJ-8 Scrambler from the '80s is designed to handle high-speed off-road racing. Tim Kuniskis, head of American Brands and SRT Performance, said that the concept shows what happens when "SRT stops treating the trail as the limit and builds the ultimate open-air desert weapon".

While the new Scrambler shares the ladder-frame chassis with the Wrangler, it comes with an all-new independent front suspension system, developed with help from off-road racing champion Casey Currie. This setup is a first for the Wrangler and is combined with a "trophy-truck-inspired rear axle" promising "stability, steering precision, and wheel control for high-speed off-road driving".

The concept also rides on bronze beadlock wheels shod in large off-road tires, contributing to a generous ground clearance and a wide stance. Jeep didn't share the detailed specifications of the powertrain, but confirmed it is a V8, hinting at a Hellcat-sourced supercharged 6.2-liter Hemi.

Visually, the new Scrambler adopts a two-door pickup body style with a removable roof and a striking Punk'n orange shade. The front end features a retro-flavored sharknose grille treatment, similar to earlier Easter Jeep Safari concepts such as the Wrangler Anvil 715 from 2026 and the Convoy from 2025.

The profile is characterized by a higher beltline, longer doors, SRT badges on the side gills, and a thick B-pillar which is shaped like a sports bar. At the back, we find a tailgate with Scrambler lettering, Wrangler-sourced LED taillights, and integrated steps on the rear bumper.

The rear bed has a structural roll cage and a spray-applied liner. It also houses bench seats that rotate 180 degrees for passengers who prefer facing rearward. The seats can also be fully removed, allowing for greater cargo capacity.

The cabin is upholstered in Dark Graphite leather with orange inserts and stitching, bronze details, and plenty of SRT logos. Other custom touches include the new grab handles and the rear-seat Jeep Multi-panel System.

article_paragraphs: It takes more than stickers and big tires to drive off-road, and Hyundai hopes its new Palisade XRT Pro has what it takes to venture further

Take a look around the world of off-road-themed SUVs , and you'll notice a trend. Plenty of them feature cool graphics. Some get bright, flashy tow hooks. Very few get a lift kit and a serious skid plate. And that last bit is key because there's a sound that can signal just how legitimate your off-road package is.

At Rush Springs Ranch, it came from underneath the Hyundai Palisade XRT Pro as its skid plate met the terrain. Suddenly, the most interesting part of this three-row family SUV was a piece of hardware most owners will hopefully never need. And, for those listening closely, it signifies a shift for this badge.

Most of the Palisade's existence has been about making the argument that skipping a luxury badge makes sense. It's always offered comfort, space, and enough equipment that considerably more expensive SUVs look a tad greedy. Sure, general adventure was a part of the pitch, but it was a tiny piece.

With the Palisade XRT Pro, that's all changing. All-terrain tires, additional ground clearance, underbody protection, and an electronic limited-slip rear differential add serious hardware to the badge. We drove it on pavement and off-road to find out how much those changes actually matter.
Full disclosure: Hyundai put me up for a couple of nights in a swanky Bentonville Hotel and fed me while I checked out the Palisade XRT Pro and Tucson XRT.
Hyundai provided travel and accommodations to Pineville, Missouri to drive the Palisade XRT Pro and Tucson XRT. CarScoops' opinions are our own.

The current Palisade already has plenty of design cues that contribute to an off-road-focused trim. The broad nose, tall body , and very pronounced lighting signatures give it presence. Importantly, that's all before the XRT Pro treatments enter the equation. Plenty of automakers settle for trying to sell ruggedness with black badging and a fun name.

title: Hyundai's XRT Off-Road Division Is On The Right Path But A Step Behind
raw_summary: There's nothing more in vogue right now than automakers soft-roader-ing their crossovers for weekend warrior types who enjoy a bit of camping or a dirt road every once in a while. Honda has TrailSport, Subaru has Wilderness, Toyota has TRD, GMC has AT4, and so on and so forth. Of course one of the largest automakers in the U.S. would want to get in on the action, so Hyundai spun up its own off-road sub-brand a few years back: XRT, which stands for Extreme Rugged Terrain. What started out as more of a trim and appearance package on vehicles like the first-gen Palisade and fourth-gen Tucson and Santa Fe has evolved into offering styling changes with a bit of added capability when the going gets bumpy. With the introduction of Hyundai's XRT Pro trim on the Palisade and upcoming fifth-gen Tucson , that idea gets taken up another notch. However, after spending a day with both the 2026 Santa Fe XRT and 2026 Palisade XRT Pro off-roading in rural Missouri, I'm not totally sure Hyundai is all the way there yet. That's not to say the Korean automaker isn't on the right path and won't keep improving expeditiously, but as it stands right now, it may be just a step or two behind.
