article_paragraphs: There's nothing more in vogue right now than automakers soft-roader-ing their crossovers for weekend warrior types who enjoy a bit of camping or a dirt road every once in a while. Honda has TrailSport, Subaru has Wilderness, Toyota has TRD, GMC has AT4, and so on and so forth. Of course one of the largest automakers in the U.S. would want to get in on the action, so Hyundai spun up its own off-road sub-brand a few years back: XRT, which stands for Extreme Rugged Terrain.

What started out as more of a trim and appearance package on vehicles like the first-gen Palisade and fourth-gen Tucson and Santa Fe has evolved into offering styling changes with a bit of added capability when the going gets bumpy. With the introduction of Hyundai's XRT Pro trim on the Palisade and upcoming fifth-gen Tucson , that idea gets taken up another notch. However, after spending a day with both the 2026 Santa Fe XRT and 2026 Palisade XRT Pro off-roading in rural Missouri, I'm not totally sure Hyundai is all the way there yet. That's not to say the Korean automaker isn't on the right path and won't keep improving expeditiously, but as it stands right now, it may be just a step or two behind.
Full Disclosure: Hyundai flew me out to Bentonville, Arkansas, put me up in a very nice hotel and fed me, all so I could sample the 2026 Santa Fe XRT and 2026 Palisade XRT Pro.

It can be sort of tricky to evaluate the capability of a soft-roader like Hyundai's XRT fleet. Technically, both the Palisade XRT Pro and Santa Fe XRT were able to do everything that was thrown at them on this program, but they both lacked a bit of the sure-footedness I just experienced in Honda's Passport TrailSport , and that was on a far more technical and challenging course. That being said, what I did with the XRT siblings is probably 10 times as grueling as what the average Hyundai owner will do with their SUVs. There's also the issue of tires. While the Passport TrailSport is fitted with beefy General Grabber A/T Sport all-terrain rubber, the Santa Fe XRT makes do with less-aggressive Continental TerrainContact A/Ts, which leads to a good bit of wheel slippage.

Still, both XRTs do an admirable job of tackling trails, though rock crawlers they are not. The Palisade XRT Pro I drove was certainly the more capable of the two, thanks to its electronic limited-slip differential in the rear and a 360-degree camera that helped overcome its sheer size, but it never felt particularly at home, even if it did tackle every obstacle without much protest.

I say much protest because, while the car didn't get stuck at any point, the 4,575-pound crossover didn't exactly seem happy, and that especially goes for its Hyundai-built 8-speed transmission. While the naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V6 provided enough power (287 horsepower and 260 pound-feet of torque) to get up just about anything despite a lack of low-end oomph, I could tell that the 8-speed was none too pleased. I couldn't hear it on the road, but when switching to the Sand setting in its Trail drive mode, there was a noticeable whine coming from it on the throttle. A temperature readout in the gauge cluster also served as a constant reminder it was, uh, hot, and when I got out of the car, there was an unmistakable smell of hot transmission wafting through the air. From a functional standpoint, the XRT Pro didn't skip a beat, which is certainly a testament to the rest of the Palisade's drivetrain and its 8.4 inches of ground clearance; it bottomed out far less than I expected it to.

It's a similar story with the Santa Fe XRT. It may lack the e-LSD and all-out grunt of the Palisade , but it does make up for that somewhat with more low-end grunt courtesy of a torquey turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-4 that pumps out 277 hp and 311 lb-ft of torque. This drivetrain lent itself far better to the old-school way of getting yourself unstuck: give 'er some gas. Sure, there are 10 fewer horses than the Palisade's V6, but an extra 51 torques is massive.

Still, you can tell the Santa Fe is a far less luxury-oriented product than the Palisade , and I got bumped around a hell of a lot more than I did in the Palisade. Obviously, there's a price delta to consider, as the Santa Fe XRT starts at $43,940 including destination, and the Palisade XRT Pro has a far more costly $51,820 entrance price.

title: Former CAKE team is back in the kitchen with a new electric motorcycle
raw_summary: If the new ReBake Abler electric motorcycle looks like it might share a bit of DNA with Sweden’s dearly departed CAKE, there’s a good reason for that. ReBake Motors has officially unveiled its first electric two-wheeler at EICMA 2026 in Milan, introducing the Abler as a highly modular, utility-focused electric moped and light motorcycle.
summary: If the new ReBake Abler electric motorcycle looks like it might share a bit of DNA with Sweden’s dearly departed CAKE, there’s a good reason for that. ReBake Motors has officially unveiled its first electric two-wheeler at EICMA 2026 in Milan, introducing the Abler as a highly modular, utility-focused electric moped and light motorcycle.
article_paragraphs: If the new ReBake Abler electric motorcycle looks like it might share a bit of DNA with Sweden’s dearly departed CAKE, there’s a good reason for that.
ReBake Motors has officially unveiled its first electric two-wheeler at EICMA 2026 in Milan, introducing the Abler as a highly modular, utility-focused electric moped and light motorcycle.

Behind the new Swedish company is founder and CEO Karl Ytterborn, who spent eight years at CAKE from its founding in 2016 through 2024. CAKE famously built some of the most interesting minimalist electric motorcycles and utility bikes on the market before ultimately collapsing after failing to secure additional funding. Ytterborn says ReBake is intended to apply many of the lessons learned during that experience, while eliminating unnecessary cost and complexity.

Its chunky 42mm aluminum tube frame isn’t just a styling exercise. ReBake designed it as a mounting system, allowing cargo accessories to attach directly to the frame at multiple locations. That means riders can configure the bike for everything from carrying groceries and passengers to more serious utility duties.
There are two versions. The Abler45 is an EU L1e-B moped with a 45 km/h (28 mph) top speed, 4 kW nominal motor and 5.12 kW peak output. It starts at €3,990 including VAT.

The €4,990 Abler80 steps up to the A1 light motorcycle category, increasing nominal power to 6.14 kW and peak power to 7.68 kW while pushing the top speed beyond 80 km/h (50 mph). Both versions use a direct-drive rear hub motor.

Energy comes from removable 2 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries weighing 17 kg (37.5 lb) apiece. The Abler45 comes standard with one battery but can carry two, while the Abler80 includes two for 4 kWh of total capacity. With both batteries, ReBake claims up to 160 km (99 miles) of low-speed urban range on the Abler45 or 114 km (71 miles) on the Abler80. Each battery can be charged either on or off the bike from a normal 230V outlet, reaching a full charge in four hours.

The rest of the hardware includes 14-inch cast wheels, 140mm of front suspension travel, dual rear shocks, front and rear disc brakes with combined braking, regenerative braking, and full LED lighting.

title: The reason behind Honda's power unit lasting five laps in Mexico GP

article_paragraphs: In its Mexico Grand Prix preview, Honda’s Shintaro Orihara had described Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez as “a very challenging track for the power unit”, but he perhaps didn’t expect Aston Martin’s weekend to go so awry.

Despite decent pace and mileage in free practice – Fernando Alonso was just 0.769s down on pacesetter Charles Leclerc in FP2, with the AMR26s covering a whopping 144 laps across all three sessions – it all went wrong in the competitive sessions.

Honda did fix some driveability and turbo lag issues between FP3 and qualifying, but Alonso encountered “abnormal signals on the water systems” on Saturday afternoon, which didn’t prevent him from outqualifying Lance Stroll ; still, both cars were out in Q1, four tenths down on the Q2 cut-off time.
In the race, the pair retired after five laps due to cooling issues.

“We knew that with the special high-altitude circumstance of Mexico City, we would face some additional challenges compared to other racetracks for the cooling,” said Orihara, Honda’s trackside general manager and chief engineer, following the race.
“However, we found that our ERS cooling circuit was under heavier stress than anticipated and this is why we had to stop the car in different sessions.
“Despite completing a series of laps during the practice sessions, the issue occurred today and during qualifying yesterday.

“At each race this year, we need to learn for 2027, even the hard lessons. We have a lot of data that we can bring back to this circuit next year, including on the turbo lag, and we will work on the solutions.”

article_paragraphs: Alpina's new era under the BMW Group umbrella has already started, with the sleek BMW Vision Alpina concept that debuted earlier this year serving as an indication of what to expect. Now, the sub-brand is ready to unveil a new production model, sharing the first official teaser on social media.

The single photo shows a low-slung sedan with split LED headlights. While the teaser intentionally blurs the bodywork in a flash of speed, we already know it is the Alpina version of the facelifted BMW 7-Series . The model will crown the flagship sedan lineup and will be followed by a similar version of the next BMW X7 SUV.

The post arrived with a subtle caption suggesting that testing is already underway: "You may have already passed it. The next BMW ALPINA is on the road. #ElevatingJourneys #BMWALPINA". Indeed, our spy photographers have caught camouflaged prototypes based on the 7-Series, revealing several styling differences compared to the standard and M-branded versions.

Based on the teaser and spy shots, the new Alpina 7er will feature amber DRLs, following the earlier concept. It is also expected to adopt a unique front-bumper design, with a more prominent splitter and a new pattern for the kidney grille.
Other Alpina-specific features will include a new set of alloy wheels, special emblems, the signature oval-shaped quad tailpipes, and quite possibly new color options.

According to the Bavarian automaker, BMW Alpina will play a different role in its lineup than the M Division. Besides performance, the sub-brand will focus on comfort and luxury, bridging the gap between high-end BMW models and Rolls-Royce. In other words, it will serve as a direct rival to offerings from the Mercedes-Maybach division. This is why the new era will begin with the 7-Series and the X7, likely offering more personalization options than the existing BMW Individual catalog.

Judging from the sound of BMW Alpina 7-Series prototypes during track testing, the successor of the discontinued B7 will have a V8 engine under the hood. For context, the pre-facelift 760i xDrive came fitted with a mild-hybrid twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8 generating 536 hp (400 kW / 544 PS).

Still, the lineup might also include a fully electric option, likely borrowing the most potent dual-motor powertrain from the i7 M70, which is rated at 670 hp (500 kW / 680 PS). In any case, the Alpina logo is expected to bring exterior, interior, and chassis modifications, further elevating the experience of driving or being driven at the Autobahn.

When you think of Wrangler, what's the first thing to come to mind? Is it the legendary Jeep that debuted during WWII? Or is it the brand of blue jeans originally designed for rodeo wear and that are just as old? It's unusual for two brands to leverage the same name, even when they serve different categories. The main corporate concern is that one brand's failure might possibly taint the other's fortunes.

That wasn't a primary concern when we considered the 2003 Jeep Wrangler Sahara that came our way on Monday. A bit battered, but not beyond redemption, the Wrangler (Jeep, not jeans) came with a factory hardtop and a $7,500 asking price. You all mostly liked what you saw and weren't too perturbed by the price. That combo earned the Wrangler (Jeep, not jeans) a narrow but ultimately victorious 55% 'Nice Price' nod.

Not everyone knows the difference between four-wheel drive and all-wheel drive. They sound similar and interchangeable, but the terms describe distinct drivetrains, each designed for specific purposes. The Jeep we looked at yesterday was 4WD, a drivetrain that ties all four wheels together when needed through a central locking differential for low-speed maneuvering through mud and over rocks.

By contrast, today's 2001 Audi A4 Quattro Avant is permanently activated AWD and is intended not for off-roading but for more secure handling and power application in inclement weather. For Audi, at least, this drivetrain is time-tested and rally-proven. Their personalities are further differentiated by their looks: the Jeep being brutish and basic while the Audi is one of the most handsome and elegant small estates ever offered for sale.

This one, in Cactus Green with the coal mine black interior that was favored by German carmakers back in the day, comes with a clean title, 175,020 miles under its Cactus Green belt, and an extensive list of refurbishment and renewal that has left it looking like Cinderella before the ball.

Under the A4's hood is a 20-valve version of Volkswagen/Audi's ubiquitous inline four, here in 1.8-liter displacement, denoted as the "AJL". Turbocharged and intercooled, the engine makes 170 horsepower and 166 pound-feet of torque. That's routed through a five-speed automatic with Tiptronic manual controls on both the lever and steering wheel for when the driver is feeling a little spicy. Naturally, as a Quattro, it sends torque to all four wheels via a central viscous diff. We'll get to more on the mechanical situation in a sec, but first, let's address the car's appearance.

Overall, this little Audi looks to be in great condition for its age and not insignificant miles. The paint still shines; there are no significant dings or dents beneath that top coat, and the headlamp lenses show only minor clouding. According to the seller, they addressed minor paint imperfections, including bumper scrapes and hatch scratches. Surprisingly, the interior is in even better shape, looking almost as-new thanks to several replacement parts and general care and cleaning. Even the comically flimsy dashboard cup holder appears to be working as originally intended.

There's still work to be done, but the seller advises that it will come with a service manual to ease the burden.
Let's see how burdensome we find its price.

article_paragraphs: It'd be nice if it was available on the all-wheel drive variant, but we won't complain

Annual model year announcements often end up with plenty of PR speak and, ultimately, much ado about nothing. Frankly, several of them end up downright disappointing when long-loved enthusiast features disappear, prices climb, or both happen. Thankfully, Mazda has some great news as we head into 2027. Its compact hatchback will continue to offer a six-speed manual, and buyers who choose it get a few extra comforts this time around.

According to Mazda's pricing and packaging announcement, the manual moves into the 2.5 S Premium Plus hatchback. It starts at $31,950, or $33,265 with the $1,315 destination charge. That's $300 more than the outgoing manual-equipped Premium, which makes the additional equipment a little easier to appreciate. Of course, that doesn't mean that the gargantuan caveats of the past are gone.

Those who insist on three pedals have to forego all-wheel drive and can't get a turbo either. Those are, in our eyes, gigantic misses from Mazda as both the turbo engine and AWD setup each have their own benefits. Combining them with a stick would be near enough to a MazdaSpeed3 that we might be willing to quit begging for it. Still, Mazda is giving those who love to drive one more reason to keep considering this car.

The manual pairs with Mazda's naturally aspirated 2.5-liter four-cylinder, producing 186 hp (139 kW) and 186 lb-ft (252 Nm) of torque on regular gasoline. As we've covered in previous reviews, it's not a fast powertrain, but it's great in pretty much every setting except high-speed highway passes. For 2027, Mazda adds a few cabin benefits.

The Premium Plus hatchback gets a 10.25-inch center display with touchscreen functionality for Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and a heated steering wheel. A windshield-projected head-up display, adaptive headlights that swivel through corners, and signature LED lighting front and rear are also standard. Keep in mind, the heated wheel and display size are upgrades from the previous base manual Mazda 3.

Overall, the Mazda3 improves in standard equipment. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto now come standard on the Select Sport, while Preferred adds wireless phone charging. The Preferred hatchback adds an AWD option priced at $29,990, though destination charges push the actual starting sticker to $31,305. Notably, the Base 2.5 S is no longer available.

That makes the Select Sport at $27,040 the new entry point and about $1,390 more than in 2026. On the flip side, front-drive Preferred hatchbacks now start at $28,040, which is actually $600 less than the outgoing version. Sedan buyers can keep the base 2.5 S, now priced at $24,750, and add a Premium AWD trim with leather upholstery and a 12-speaker Bose stereo. title: How Antonelli demolished Russell in the same car
raw_summary: Kimi Antonelli's historic Formula 1 title run is complete and so too is his crushing of team-mate George Russell in 2026's major script-flip. Having gone toe-to-toe with Lewis Hamilton in their three years as team-mates, and even ended with a clear edge over the seven-time world champion, Russell started 2026 by blitzing the season opener in Australia.

article_paragraphs: Kimi Antonelli's historic Formula 1 title run is complete and so too is his crushing of team-mate George Russell in 2026's major script-flip.

Having gone toe-to-toe with Lewis Hamilton in their three years as team-mates, and even ended with a clear edge over the seven-time world champion, Russell started 2026 by blitzing the season opener in Australia.

With Mercedes starting the new rules era with the advantage we all expected, it looked like the stars were aligning for him. Instead, just over seven months later, the title officially went to Antonelli four rounds early - and a distraught Russell still does not really know how.

As good as Russell's peaks have been, the end result is embarrassing: beaten by a second-year driver eight years his junior. Antonelli's won nine races to Russell's three, is 130 points ahead, and has wrapped it all up four rounds early. These are not championship contender numbers from Russell, they are number two numbers, and he is the first to admit his performances have not been good enough.
But why not, and why have his high points been so infrequent? These have been the key questions asked by Russell himself, not just everybody watching.

If it was so easy to identify exactly what's not working for Russell, he and Mercedes would have spotted it and fixed it. But analysing every session this year, dozens of laps and hundreds of data points, not to mention quizzing the two protagonists throughout the year, has enabled us to produce some key informed theories.
First: qualifying. Russell's previous reputation in F1 was Mr Saturday but Antonelli has definitively turned the tables here, even though his advantage is actually quite narrow in volume.

There are 109 sessions we have been able to compare across practice and each qualifying segment in 2026, and Antonelli is ahead in 58 of them compared to 51 for Russell. But practice sessions don't mean as much as qualifying. And where it really matters, which is in Q3, or SQ3 on sprint weekends, the median average gap is just under two tenths of a second in Antonelli's favour, standing at 0.185 seconds.

title: 2,977 HP U9 Xtreme Destroyed As BYD Aims For 311 MPH
raw_summary: Lat year, BYD's Yangwang U9 Xtreme eclipsed the top speed of the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+ when the Chinese supercar hit 308.4 mph (496.22 kph) at the ATP high-speed test track in Papenburg, Germany. But BYD wasn't satisfied. During that run, telemetry data showed the driver had enough space to keep the throttle pinned for an extra 1.5 seconds, which may have been enough to squeeze a little extra speed from the Yangwang U9 . BYD is now preparing for another speed run in the UAE later this month with the hopes of topping 311 mph (500 km/h), and a recently released behind-the-scenes video shows what kind of danger lurks during the preparation for such a feat. The force of the impacts ripped the U9 Xtreme to shreds, leaving little left but the carbon fiber monocoque. Fortunately, the driver escaped without any major injuries.

It's not clear when this incident occurred, and it may have even been before last year's 308.4-mph top speed run in Germany. Regardless, it appears the Chinese brand used the accident as a valuable lesson in how best to set up the car for such speeds, but it wasn't the only problem the team needed to overcome. During testing in China, BYD's engineers were optimizing the U9 Xtreme for high-speed driving when they ran into issues once the car exceeded 253 mph (400 km/h). At these speeds, the car experienced a wobble, which obviously isn't ideal. BYD traced this issue back to some of the test equipment placed on the vehicles, forcing it to remove them before continuing the tests.

Back in July, BYD vice president Stella Li confirmed the company's plan to exceed the 311 mph (500 km/h) barrier with the U9 Xtreme, although the company hasn't confirmed an exact date or pinpointed a specific road. High-speed tests like this are usually conducted at private testing facilities, although finding one isn't easy. Koenigsegg last ran a noteworthy top-speed test on a public road on an 11-mile stretch of Nevada State Route 160 between Pahrump and Las Vegas in 2017. In this test, the Agera RS recorded a two-way top speed average of 277.87 mph (446.97 km/h), making it the world's fastest production car at the time. If the Yangwang achieves its 311-mph goal, it will be almost 13% faster than the Koenigsegg.

title: It Took 5,500 Hours For Ringbrothers To Build This Wild Pontiac GTO
raw_summary: Wisconsin-based Ringbrothers has established itself as an expert in classic American muscle car retromods , and whenever the SEMA Show rolls around, we know it'll have something special up its sleeve. article_paragraphs: Wisconsin-based Ringbrothers has established itself as an expert in classic American muscle car retromods , and whenever the SEMA Show rolls around, we know it'll have something special up its sleeve. Arguably the most significant changes are beneath the skin . Ringbrothers built Billie around a special Fast Track Stage III chassis from Roadster Shop, featuring Fox coilovers and almighty six-piston Brembo brakes up front and in the rear. These components should be enough to ensure this Pontiac drives more like a modern car than one that dates back more than 60 years. It also includes custom 1.25-inch sway bars, C7 Corvette end links, and bespoke upper and lower front control arms.

Then there's the engine. Ringbrothers has sourced an LT4 crate engine from Wegner Motorsports rated at 650 horsepower and 650 pound-feet of torque. Original GTO Convertibles maxed out at 360 hp when new, so you can probably understand the importance of the new suspension and braking components. In addition, a new Bowler Performance 10L90E automatic transmission has been fitted, sending power through the rear wheels.

To give the car some hope of putting its power to the ground, custom 19-inch front and 20-inch HRE wheels have been fitted, wrapped in 295/35 front and 345/30 rear Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires. Even with all that rubber, we suspect this thing will leave thick, black lines of rubber wherever it gets driven.

The original GTO was completely stripped back as part of the rebuild, and a custom body kit was formed, so the car now sits five inches wider than it used to. Complementing the butch new look are extended rocker panels, a carbon fiber hood with an enlarged scoop, and a distinctive new front grille. Billet machined aluminum also appears on the taillight panel and parts of the hood.

Continuing the exterior modifications are redesigned carbon fiber and steel door skins, a carbon fiber front lower valance, and a carbon fiber rear diffuser, plus a unique rear bumper. Despite the significance of all these exterior modifications, Billie keeps that classic Pontiac vibe. Making it really shimmer is a custom shade of Billie Goat Blue paint from BASF Glasurit.

No project like this would be complete without an interior to match the exterior. It was expertly crafted by Upholstery Unlimited, and the entire dashboard has been pushed forward four inches and sits two inches lower. The cabin is dominated by newly wrapped leather, 3D-printed speaker grilles, and the original factory radio unit has been modified to include Bluetooth. The gear shifter is rather interesting and is actually a modified portafilter from a coffee machine. Dynamat was called in to provide the sound deadening, and a new black soft top has also been fitted.

Rewind a few years ago, and it seemed as though the SRT Hellcat model would be a short-lived special given how long the Durango has been in production . Dodge introduced it for the 2021 model year and then dropped it just 12 months later. At the time, it seemed destined for the history books. Thankfully, it made a triumphant return in 2023 and has served as an important flagship for the aging SUV ever since.

This particular Durango SRT Hellcat was recently handed over to the Texas Department of Public Safety's North Texas Region. It doesn't have a 'look-at-me' colorful livery like those exotic police cars found in Dubai . Instead, it's dominated by black paint with ghosted graphics on the sides. What sets it apart from a typical Hellcat that a local Texan might own is a black bull bar and all the flashing blue and red lights you'd expect on a police cruiser.

It's unclear if Texas authorities will use this Dodge on patrol, or if it'll simply be a showpiece. If it's the latter, it would join a long list of high-end police cruisers used at community events to not only promote a local department, but also help foster healthy relationships between police and the community they serve. With a burbling supercharged V8 and 710 horsepower, a Durango SRT Hellcat is a surefire way to appeal to Texas enthusiasts.

In August 2025, Dodge announced it was ditching the naturally aspirated 3.6-liter V6 that had been available on the Durango, and moving forward, would only sell the SUV with its 5.7-liter and 6.4-liter Hemi V8s, in addition to the supercharged 6.2-liter V8 of the Hellcat. For several months, the 6.4-liter and Hellcat models were banned in the country's 17 CARB-regulated states, but Dodge quickly updated the Durango to comply with local regulations.

raw_summary: The Chinese brand is trialling an updated base SU7 Ultra alongside its winged Nürburgring lap record contender China's Xiaomi has been back at the Nürburgring honing a dramatic aero package for the SU7 Ultra sedan that it hopes will help it reclaim its production EV lap record from Porsche. summary: The Chinese brand is trialling an updated base SU7 Ultra alongside its winged Nürburgring lap record contender China's Xiaomi has been back at the Nürburgring honing a dramatic aero package for the SU7 Ultra sedan that it hopes will help it reclaim its production EV lap record from Porsche.
article_paragraphs: The Chinese brand is trialling an updated base SU7 Ultra alongside its winged Nürburgring lap record contender

China's Xiaomi has been back at the Nürburgring honing a dramatic aero package for the SU7 Ultra sedan that it hopes will help it reclaim its production EV lap record from Porsche. But while most eyes have naturally been drawn to the huge rear spoiler on one camouflaged prototype, another Xiaomi test car without a wing has been quietly flying under the radar.

Fresh spy shots from Germany show Xiaomi isn't only testing a high downforce version of its top-spec electric sedan, but is also putting a regular SU7 Ultra without the optional track kit through its paces. It misses out on the giant fixed, motorsport-style spoiler and the aggressive rear diffuser, though it does have an active spoiler that pops up from the trunk lid above 50 mph (80 kmh) to provide downforce. We can't see any obvious changes between this SU7 Ultra prototype and the model that's already on sale, but it's possible Xiaomi is planning some changes under the skin that could make it even more powerful.

The stock SU7 Ultra is hardly lacking in the firepower department. It makes a massive 1,526 (1547 PS/ 1139 kW) from a triple-motor setup that places one motor at the front axle, and two at the rear. That powertrain was a key enabler when the Ultra set the EV production car lap record at the Ring in 2025 with a time of 7:04.957, beating the Porsche Taycan Turbo, and even the Rimac Nevera hypercar, in the process.

But in 2024 Xiaomi showed a quad-motor EV platform with a silly 1,526 (1547 PS/ 1139 kW), suggesting it's hungry to push power outputs even harder. And even if the SU7 Ultra doesn't switch to a quad motor powertrain – which may be saved for an upcoming coupe – Xiaomi could find a few more horses to help it claim back its Ring crown from Porsche.

Porsche enlisted Manthey's assistance to come up with a performance package for the Taycan Turbo GT that goes above and beyond the no-back-seat Weissach kit already available on the GT. With more aggressive aero, and arch extensions covering a wider track, plus a small power boost, the Manthey Taycan ticked off a blistering 6:55.553 time in May of this year to take the Ring EV record. It still counts as a production car because the upgrade is available through Porsche dealers, Porsche owning a stake in the Nürburg-based motorsport company. But it might not be the Nürburgring production EV lap record holder for much longer, if Xiaomi gets its way.

article_paragraphs: After completing the first half of the Bellefield complex last summer , Maximo engineers have put their helpful robot friend into high gear, with the latest version 3.0 robot-equipped construction crews installing as many as 24 solar panel modules per hour, per person. And now, the company is reporting that Maximo has completed its 300,000th construction task. (!)

If that 24 modules per hour, per person rate sounds fast, that’s because it is . At full tilt, the latest Maximo robot-equipped crews have nearly doubled the output of traditional installation methods at similar solar locations throughout Southern California. Now, with 300,000 tasks under its belt , the robot is proving to be both fast and durable.
“The future of solar construction depends on bringing together the experience of our people and new technology,” explains Matt Tetrault, President of Primoris’ Renewables business.

Like just about everyone these days, Maximo is playing up its machines’ NVDIVIA hardware, re-branding its robots’ repetitive automation as “physical AI.” That’s not to say the robots don’t work, however – as their deployment at Amazon’s Bellefield solar field is proving.

(By) leveraging NVIDIA AI infrastructure together with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries and NVIDIA Isaac Sim open robotics simulation framework, the Maximo team was able to develop, test and refine robotic capabilities through physics-based simulation and AI driven modeling before deploying updates in the field. The combination of AI, vision, robotics and simulation driven engineering reduced development and validation timelines and increased confidence in field performance as the robotic fleet scaled.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) powered the development, deployment, and operation of Maximo’s AI-driven field systems. AWS provides scalable computing, automated software delivery, and advanced data analytics, including real-time construction intelligence, enabling Maximo to collect operational robotics data and continuously improve performance.

The rapid deployment of solar panels at utility scale projects like this one, which is set to eventually reach over a GW of solar generating capacity , will help companies like Amazon reduce their carbon footprint, of course – but also save them big money as the price of fossil fuels continues to climb .

The Maximo team says it has plans to extend its robots potential use cases beyond solar and into construction tasks that require similar pick and place and feeding and attaching movements, site logistics, and site cleanup. And like just about every other business that demands a high degree of physical labor, the construction industry is facing huge labor shortages, making machines like Maximo that provide real efficiency gains welcome additions to the job site .

raw_summary: This is the Plymouth Fireball 500 by Barris Kustom, it was built as Frankie Avalon’s character’s hero car for the 1966 film also named “Fireball 500.” The car wasn’t just a show pony, when new it was said to be powered by a 426 cubic inch (7.0 liter) Hemi V8 mated to a 4-speed manual gearbox, and it had a reported top speed of over 160 mph – a highly-respectable achievement in the mid-1960s.

article_paragraphs: This is the Plymouth Fireball 500 by Barris Kustom, it was built as Frankie Avalon’s character’s hero car for the 1966 film also named “Fireball 500.”

The car wasn’t just a show pony, when new it was said to be powered by a 426 cubic inch (7.0 liter) Hemi V8 mated to a 4-speed manual gearbox, and it had a reported top speed of over 160 mph – a highly-respectable achievement in the mid-1960s.

When it was first built by George Barris, the Fireball 500 was powered by a 426 cubic inch (7.0 liter) Hemi V8, with a 4-speed manual transmission. The car was essentially a heavily-rebuilt 1966 Plymouth Barracuda that had been ordered by American International Pictures from Barris in late 1965 and Chrysler supplied the donor car. Interestingly, Barris was turning a Lincoln Futura concept car into the Batmobile at the same time in the same garage.
This is the “Fireball 500” by Barris Kustom, it was built for Frankie Avalon as the hero car for the 1966 film also named “Fireball 500.”

The first-gen Barracuda was a fastback version of the Plymouth Valiant, launched in April of 1964 with a curved 14.4 square foot rear window. As cool as that rear screen might have been, Barris didn’t need it, so he removed it, along with the roof.

In their place his team built two separate cockpits, each had its own cowl hand-formed from metal and a curved windshield made from butyrate plastic. Flared headrests were added around each cockpit opening and ran back into the rear bodywork. There, four razor-edged fins were molded as a single metal section covering what had been the rear seat and trunk lid. It was a wild looking car, even before the paintwork was applied.

The rear fenders were extended and the vertical taillights were lengthened by four inches, rectangular headlights imported from France sat in a reworked grille up front. The wheel wells were enlarged for 700/12.50-13 Firestone tires on 13-inch spoked alloy wheels, side exhausts built from Reynolds aluminum extrusions ran along the rockers, and eight air-intake tubes sat in the hood. Inside, a 13-inch deep-dish steering wheel was fitted as it suited the tight dimensions of the cockpit.

The paint was called Fireheat, it required 40 coats of hand-rubbed lacquer shaded from pearl white through to gold and tangerine to candy red and finally burgundy. It’s said that four men spent six days spraying it, layer after layer.

title: Red Bull's key strategy call behind Verstappen's Mexico win
raw_summary: Although Sunday at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez was above all Kimi Antonelli's day, there were naturally two other major storylines in the Formula 1 paddock: the tensions at Ferrari and how Fred Vasseur will manage them, plus Max Verstappen's sixth victory in Mexico. When the latter came up in the post-race press conference, the Dutchman immediately joked: "Yeah, they should actually call it the ‘Maxico’ Grand Prix. That would be great."
summary: Although Sunday at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez was above all Kimi Antonelli's day, there were naturally two other major storylines in the Formula 1 paddock: the tensions at Ferrari and how Fred Vasseur will manage them, plus Max Verstappen's sixth victory in Mexico. article_paragraphs: Although Sunday at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez was above all Kimi Antonelli's day, there were naturally two other major storylines in the Formula 1 paddock: the tensions at Ferrari and how Fred Vasseur will manage them, plus Max Verstappen's sixth victory in Mexico.
When the latter came up in the post-race press conference, the Dutchman immediately joked: "Yeah, they should actually call it the ‘Maxico’ Grand Prix. That would be great."

On a more serious note, there are several factors behind Verstappen's track record in Mexico. During Red Bull's Honda years, the Japanese manufacturer had a highly effective turbo at altitude – partly based on knowledge from the aviation industry – which often made Red Bull competitive in terms of engine performance.
In addition, Verstappen himself is particularly adept at dealing with the low-downforce conditions that traditionally make Mexico a slippery affair, with drivers sliding around even more than normal.

While Red Bull made mistakes in Austin and, according to its drivers, stuck too stubbornly to the softer compounds and was not open-minded enough to react to what was happening during the race, the opposite proved to be the case in Mexico.

Due to Charles Leclerc's five-second penalty, Red Bull immediately decided to pit at the same time, even though this was not entirely in line with its own pre-planned tyre strategy. After all, Verstappen had started on mediums and would normally have gone longer, but Red Bull understood that track position was crucial at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, where the effect of dirty air was significant and overtaking was also difficult because of the power unit regulations.

Red Bull knew that if it stayed out longer, it would give Leclerc the advantage of several laps on fresh rubber. With a later pitstop, Verstappen would therefore have rejoined the track behind Leclerc. The four-time world champion would then have had the tyre advantage, but Red Bull opted for track position, much to Verstappen's satisfaction.

"I think Charles just pulled away. I could not really stay with him,” said Verstappen. “I did not have the pace to follow him, but at the same time, I was still around that five-second window. So, then the team, I think, did a really good job to follow him in."

title: Yamaha unveils new NMAX E, bringing electric power to its popular motorbike lineup
raw_summary: Yamaha is expanding its electric two-wheeler lineup with a much more capable machine, unveiling the new NMAX E as an electric version of its popular NMAX sport scooter. The 2027 Yamaha NMAX E is being positioned as a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter, putting it firmly above the low-speed urban electric scooters that have made up much of Yamaha’s electric lineup thus far.
summary: Yamaha is expanding its electric two-wheeler lineup with a much more capable machine, unveiling the new NMAX E as an electric version of its popular NMAX sport scooter. The 2027 Yamaha NMAX E is being positioned as a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter, putting it firmly above the low-speed urban electric scooters that have made up much of Yamaha’s electric lineup thus far.
article_paragraphs: Yamaha is expanding its electric two-wheeler lineup with a much more capable machine, unveiling the new NMAX E as an electric version of its popular NMAX sport scooter.

The 2027 Yamaha NMAX E is being positioned as a 125cc-equivalent electric scooter, putting it firmly above the low-speed urban electric scooters that have made up much of Yamaha’s electric lineup thus far.

At its heart is Yamaha’s new compact eAxle drive unit, which sends power to the rear wheel through a belt drive. The electric motor produces 6.7 kW (9 hp) of nominal power and peaks at 7.5 kW (10 hp), along with 33.3 Nm (24.6 lb-ft) of torque.
Yamaha hasn’t published a top speed in the specifications, but the NMAX E’s A1 classification puts it in the same general category as 125cc combustion scooters rather than urban mopeds.

Power comes from a centrally mounted 3.5 kWh lithium-ion battery, which Yamaha says provides up to 104 km (65 miles) of range on the WMTC Class 1 testing cycle. The L-shaped battery is mounted low and centrally in the chassis to help maintain a low center of gravity.

Unlike many electric scooters that rely on removable batteries, the NMAX E uses a fixed pack. Yamaha has compensated for that with an onboard 800W charger, allowing riders to plug the scooter directly into a household outlet or an AC Type 2 public charging station. A full 0-100% charge takes around 5.5 hours.

Riders can choose between three riding modes. Sport (S) mode offers the quickest acceleration, Touring (T) provides smoother power delivery for everyday riding and carrying a passenger, and Eco (E) reduces acceleration and top speed while maximizing range. Regenerative braking is also included.

The rest of the scooter is fairly well equipped, including traction control, ABS, 245mm front and rear disc brakes, 13-inch wheels, a 33mm fork, dual rear shocks, and even a reverse mode to make low-speed maneuvering easier.

title: Tested: 2027 Genesis GV60 Magma Is a Riot
raw_summary: The Genesis brand’s first performance variant isn’t subtle, particularly when painted in its signature Magma Orange hue. That’s appropriate, because when driving the Magma, there might as well be a persistent devilish presence on your shoulder whispering, “Push harder.” The smirks on our faces when driving the Magma are mostly about its immensely swift acceleration, satisfying ride and handling, or the silly-but-impressive 9000-rpm fake engine noises. article_paragraphs: The Genesis brand’s first performance variant isn’t subtle, particularly when painted in its signature Magma Orange hue. And the ends of its rear wing are turned up, which, to us, gives a devil’s-horns vibe. That’s appropriate, because when driving the Magma, there might as well be a persistent devilish presence on your shoulder whispering, “Push harder.”

The smirks on our faces when driving the Magma are mostly about its immensely swift acceleration, satisfying ride and handling, or the silly-but-impressive 9000-rpm fake engine noises. But the name of this new subbrand also makes us think of “liquid hot magma” (in a Dr. Evil voice, of course).

The GV60 Magma is based on the excellent Hyundai Ioniq 5 N , which introduced the fake shifting and faux engine noises to this electric platform. Peak output is the same 641 horsepower as the Ioniq 5 N, but the Magma gets the full luxury treatment. In fact, the number of Magma-specific touches is staggering for such a low-volume model, including front bucket seats and black suede upholstery with orange stitching—even the key fob dons a Magma Orange shell. Although the front seats are comfortable and supportive, we were surprised to find no lumbar adjustability.
See all results for new 2027 Genesis GV60 Magma for sale near 52600

There are also plenty of Magma-specific displays in the gauge-cluster screen that have a chronograph feel to them. They include information such as the temperatures of the two motors and battery pack, as well as the 9000-rpm tachometer integrated into the speedometer display. Then there are all the configuration settings for the chassis and powertrain modes in the center screen. It’s all thoughtfully and tastefully executed. Plus, there are elements from the regular GV60 that still wow first-timers, such as the circular shifter that flips over and looks like a crystal ball when the car is parked.

While the Ioniq 5 N mimics a 7750-rpm four-cylinder with its engine cosplay, the Magma aims higher, instead playing the tune of a 9000-rpm V-6. Is it gimmicky? Absolutely. But it’s also impressively executed. And loud: With the adjustable noise level turned up all the way, the Magma’s interior volume measures 102 decibels—about the same as a Corvette ZR1X—as it rips its way repeatedly to its pseudo-9000 rpm over and over on the way to a 166-mph top speed.

Despite weighing roughly 90 pounds more, the Magma’s performance is all but identical to the Ioniq 5 N’s, with 60 mph arriving in a scant 3.0 seconds flat and a quarter-mile blitz of 11.1 seconds at 126 mph. The two run neck and neck, at least until the Magma’s longer Boost mode (15 seconds versus 10 in the Ioniq 5 N) causes it to pull ahead above 120 mph. Although there’s a Boost button on the steering wheel, helpfully, the Magma’s extra hit automatically engages when you push the accelerator all the way to the floor.

raw_title: How a 'stupid' speed limit stopped Mexican GP overtaking
title: How a 'stupid' speed limit stopped Mexican GP overtaking
raw_summary: Formula 1 drivers have got used to many quirks with the 2026 regulations, but the Mexican Grand Prix exposed one that Lewis Hamilton openly labelled “stupid”. On a track that has historically been very difficult for cars to overtake at - because of the aero and cooling compromises caused by the thinner air - things were even harder this year.
summary: Formula 1 drivers have got used to many quirks with the 2026 regulations, but the Mexican Grand Prix exposed one that Lewis Hamilton openly labelled “stupid”. On a track that has historically been very difficult for cars to overtake at - because of the aero and cooling compromises caused by the thinner air - things were even harder this year.
article_paragraphs: Formula 1 drivers have got used to many quirks with the 2026 regulations, but the Mexican Grand Prix exposed one that Lewis Hamilton openly labelled “stupid”.
On a track that has historically been very difficult for cars to overtake at - because of the aero and cooling compromises caused by the thinner air - things were even harder this year.

The final laps of the race highlighted that sufficient speed offsets were simply never there, as Hamilton tried his hardest to pick up leader Max Verstappen’s tow and make a move into Turn 1, plus further back Lando Norris was aiming to do the same with Charles Leclerc.

Even with the benefit of the extra 0.5MJ of energy a driver gets for overtake mode, and a slipstream of the long run down the start-finish straight, neither Hamilton nor Norris could get close enough to make a pass stick.

The main factor holding them back was not the high-altitude venue weakening the slipstream effect in a year when the DRS advantage has disappeared for the car behind. Instead, it was the consequence of an under-the-radar 2026 rule that has effectively seen F1 operate with a speed limit.
As part of the regulations to help manage the performance profile of the energy-starved cars down the straights, the rulebook imposed a deployment limit for the end of straights.
It was supposed to help ensure an offset of power (and therefore speed) to help overtake mode, but in Mexico it proved to be more of a hindrance.
To help manage deployment usage, energy deployment gets restricted for cars without overtake mode once they hit a certain speed.

title: $150 billion more paid by Americans for gas this year than last
raw_summary: Since the beginning of America’s war against Iran, Americans have paid an additional $150+ billion for gas and diesel than they did last year during the same time period , according to a study from Brown University. Global gas prices have risen because supply has been disrupted (Iran having one of the top oil reserves in the world). Americans are paying upwards of $6 a gallon even though American oil companies have not had their own supply chains disrupted the way crude from the Middle East has. The result? Windfall profits for big oil at the expense of American citizens.

Global gas prices have risen because supply has been disrupted (Iran having one of the top oil reserves in the world).
article_paragraphs: Since the beginning of America’s war against Iran, Americans have paid an additional $150+ billion for gas and diesel than they did last year during the same time period , according to a study from Brown University. Global gas prices have risen because supply has been disrupted (Iran having one of the top oil reserves in the world). Americans are paying upwards of $6 a gallon even though American oil companies have not had their own supply chains disrupted the way crude from the Middle East has.
The result? Windfall profits for big oil at the expense of American citizens.

In the leadup to his election in 2024, Donald Trump asked about 20 oil executives at Mar-a-Lago to raise $1 billion for his campaign, promising to reverse dozens of Biden-era regulations if elected. The industry seems not to have raised the full $1 billion, but oil interests still gave tens of millions to Trump-aligned committees. The policies put in place by the Republican party, who has had control of congress and the White House since the last election, have been very pro oil & gas, whether they were anti-EV, anti-solar, anti-energy efficiency, anti-fuel efficiency, anti-wind, or just flat out subsidies to oil and gas.

They ended many of the Biden Administration’s clean energy policies. They ended the Solar For All Program ( or tried to ). They ended residential and commercial solar tax credits. They signed Executive Order 14315 to terminate wind and solar production and investment tax credits and impose additional restrictions. They made solar development on Federal lands more difficult . On his first day in office, Trump signed a memo withdrawing federal offshore areas from new and renewed wind leasing – but the rule didn’t apply to oil and gas. They ended wind tax credits . They kneecapped the federal standards for vehicle fuel efficiency . They tried to eliminate Energy Star , a program that costs the government $32 million a year and saves Americans $14 billion a year. They weakened Home Energy Rebate programs , SPECIFICALLY stipulating that they could not be used to replace polluting gas furnaces (that increase childhood asthma by more than 15%) with energy efficient electric options. They even tried to make it illegal for future legislators to improve energy efficiency legislation. Then, as if that wasn’t enough, they just gave our tax dollars to the fossil industries , allocating about $190 billion in tax breaks and subsidies over the next decade from the OBBBA.
If this isn’t quid pro quo, I guess I don’t understand what quid pro quo is. But the Iran War took it to a whole new level.

Since it began on February 28, as Americans have spent about $150 billion more on gasoline and diesel, U.S. oil and gas companies earned more than $130 billion in profit from April through September, nearly triple what they earned a year earlier, according to the New York Times .
We can’t say the war was fought for the industry. The president has said his focus is stopping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon. But we can say who is paying at the pump and who is collecting.

Connect the dots however you like, but connect them before you vote. Add it to the roughly $50 billion that US taxpayers have directly spent on the war , and untold more that has percolated through the rest of our economy due to inflationary pressure from rising energy costs, and it’s safe to say it’s well over $200 billion that this war has cost us, alongside the unquantifiable cost in human lives and suffering.

article_paragraphs: The loss of guaranteed federal funding could stall projects that make it easier and cheaper for Americans to get where they need to go.

UPDATE: On October 27, 2026, an update to the Senate Commerce Committee’s Chopping Block report provided a state-by-state assessment of the harm to transportation systems if Congress fails to renew the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law’s $36.8 billion in advance appropriations funding. Led by Ranking Member Cantwell, the report demonstrates that these cuts will only drive increased costs for families and business across the country.

At a time when Americans are struggling to pay staggering prices at the fuel pump and the Trump administration sows uncertainty for states and communities by clawing back committed transportation infrastructure funds, Congress is moving to scale back more critical federal funding for affordable and clean transportation.

The need for consistent funding is clear: Transportation costs are the second-largest household expense in the United States, and our roads and transit infrastructure remain structurally inadequate . Nevertheless, state transportation and transit authorities are facing a significant funding cliff due to the expiration of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (BIL) on September 30, 2026. Over the past five years, the infrastructure law has provided a guaranteed pot of funding worth $36.8 billion for transportation projects. These “advanced appropriations” cover a wide breadth of programs and include large amounts of funding for clean transportation, such as electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure projects, transit, and rail investments. This funding has helped state transit and transportation authorities plan for longer-term projects and has been critical to the infrastructure law’s support of almost 70,000 unique transportation projects across the country.

But transportation funding from the infrastructure law ran out on September 30, 2026, and while Congress passed a short-term extension until December 11, 2026, it does not include these guaranteed dollars. This means that, for the three-month duration of the extension, states will lack the continuity and certainty they need to plan for both large- and small-scale infrastructure projects.

To add insult to injury, Congress also seems to be contemplating leaving this guaranteed funding out of the next transportation bill altogether. The House BUILD America 250 Act proposal, released in May, proposes cutting all advanced appropriations funding. The proposal, in fact, slashes transportation funding from current infrastructure law levels by almost 50 percent, leaving Americans without access to travel options that help defray rising costs.

Historically, transportation bills have included authorizations of two types of funding: (1) contract authority, which is supported by revenues that flow into the Highway Trust Fund and (2) general funds, which Congress has to “appropriate” and assign annually. The current infrastructure law includes another category—advanced appropriations—which makes money available in the future for certain programs without the need for any congressional action in future years, guaranteeing states and communities secure funding over the five-year bill period. This certainty allows for states to plan in advance for future projects and grant opportunities.

Any cut to this pot of money takes a sledgehammer to clean transportation programs that reduce household costs and improve the health of our communities. Particular programs at risk include the National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure program , which helps states build a national network of EV chargers; the Capital Investment Grants, a transit-related discretionary grant program; and the Reconnecting Communities Pilot, which aims to address harms caused by past transportation decisions. Also of concern are the BUILD and MEGA grants, which help support the build-out of transit, bicycle, and pedestrian infrastructure.

title: EV Owners Need To Lend Out Their Cars If They Want Regular People To Go Electric
raw_summary: Electric vehicles will probably never fully replace the internal combustion sports car , but mainstream daily drivers are living on borrowed time . It's not like anyone with no idea which wheels are powered or how many cylinders their car has cares about a missing exhaust note. But while EVs are taking off in the rest of the world , the U.S. lags behind, thanks in large part to pro-oil propaganda . People believe all sorts of myths about EVs, and I'm sorry, but short test drives won't fix it. Which means EV owners need to start acting like they have an obligation to lend friends and family their cars. A few days in an EV won't change anyone's mind if their lifestyle doesn't match what EVs currently offer, and that's fine. But if they've been tricked by a bunch of pro-oil myths, you may find that a few days with your car is all it takes to convince them that EVs are the best thing ever. Because even an hour-long test drive doesn't show you the benefits of living with a gas station in your garage. It's the kind of thing that probably requires a three-day loan at a minimum, because they have to see how it fits into their regular lives.

But if they've been tricked by a bunch of pro-oil myths, you may find that a few days with your car is all it takes to convince them that EVs are the best thing ever. Because even an hour-long test drive doesn't show you the benefits of living with a gas station in your garage. It's the kind of thing that probably requires a three-day loan at a minimum, because they have to see how it fits into their regular lives.

Ideally, the automakers would take the lead here, but that's probably not happening anytime soon. I've discussed this idea with employees at several automakers, and so far, I don't think anyone wants to take on the cost and complexity of dealing with dealerships to make longer-term test drives happen. So without the automakers, it falls on the EV owners who want to see EVs become more popular. We need to be the ones pushing our cars on people like they're the supposed free samples that Deputy D. Diggity Dawg Dawson insisted drug dealers would force me to take.

At least anecdotally, I don't know of anything more powerful for changing minds about EVs than time spent with your butt in the seat. Most recently, a friend had to replace their beloved Mazda CX-5 after someone hit them; they asked me about EVs, and almost before I knew it, they were the proud new owners of a Hyundai Ioniq 5. So they were already open to a car that would save them money on gas, but even they quickly realized the things they were worried about weren't actually a big deal.

According to the friend, who I will call Bill, "driving them is super f—ing fun," and he did not think he "would enjoy trying to max out the mi/kWh using the regenerative braking... But [he does]." After only a few days of driving an EV, someone experiencing their first EV was already realizing how strong the oil propaganda is and how much better EVs are at things beyond saving money on gas.

An example of a borrowing experience changing minds is my brother — he borrowed my Fiat for a week while he was in the process of replacing his company truck. With three (soon to be four!) kids, he was never going to buy a two-door hatchback, but he loved being able to charge at home so much that he went out and bought a non-Fiat EV. All it took was a little time living with an electric car that he didn't even have any interest in owning, and it changed his mind about EV ownership before he'd even driven a competitive one.

I know it's scary letting other people borrow your car, and I certainly wouldn't want you handing the keys to someone you know is irresponsible. But without automaker or federal support, we're going to have to do this on our own, and the best way to get people to change their minds about EVs is to get some real time with the cars. And what better way to make that happen is there than trading cars with someone for a few days? Friends and family help each other out, after all.

If you lend your car to someone who decides they probably shouldn't buy an EV, that's fine. No harm, no foul. But just think how happy you'll be if a few days if your car convinces someone they've been wrong about EVs and should actually get one. It's pretty nice, I'm not going to lie, and definitely worth the risk of letting someone you know drive your car. They quite literally sell themselves.

This is the Ford 5.2 XS Aluminator crate engine, it’s a 580 horsepower V8 with a displacement of 5.2 liters, and it’s made up of a slew of high-end parts used in Ford’s modern Shelby GT500 and GT350s.

Ford Racing debuted the “Aluminator” engine at the SEMA Show in Las Vegas in October of 2007. It was a new line of 4.6 liter aluminum crate engines sold as long blocks and short blocks, with short blocks starting at $4,500 USD.

The Aluminator name has since followed Ford’s overhead cam V8 from the 4.6 liter Modular engine to the 5.0 liter Coyote, and then to a 5.2 liter cross-plane relative of the Shelby GT350’s Voodoo V8. Every version of the Aluminator has been sold as a crate engine through Ford’s parts catalog and none have ever been fitted to a production car.

Ford’s Modular V8 entered production for the 1991 model year, and the first Aluminators were built around the aluminum 4.6 liter block from the Mustang GT, a version Ford said was stronger than any of their previous production 4.6 aluminum blocks. The naturally aspirated DOHC long block displaced 281 cubic inches (4.6 liters) and had a 10:1 compression ratio.

It had a forged steel crankshaft, forged H-beam rods, and forged pistons sitting under 2003-2004 Mustang Cobra heads and cams. The supercharged Cobra switched to a cast-iron block for 2003, and a supercharged-application Aluminator gave 2003-2004 Cobra owners an aluminum-block alternative with a lower 8.5:1 compression ratio. A 9.8:1 compression short block then followed on for the three-valve 2005-2010 Mustang GT.
Factory Five Racing lent Ford one of its Challenge Car racers as the test mule for a 4.6 Aluminator, which the company rated at more than 650 bhp.

For instance, out of the 2,000 "actively dating Americans" questioned, 73% said the way people take care of their cars and the way they take care of themselves go hand in hand. Moreover, 67% of those surveyed responded that they can tell if people have messy personal lives by looking at how messy their vehicles are. Coming at it from the other angle, 65% of the survey respondents agreed that a clean, well-ordered vehicle is a sign someone has a clean, well-ordered life.

In fact, 25% of the folks surveyed said they've ended a date early because the driver's car was dirty. The real surprise is that that number wasn't any higher. After all, some of the disgusting items survey-takers had seen in cars included at least one box with a dead cat in it, live roaches and maggots, bottles of urine, moldy milk, and that all-time classic, used condoms.

Driving a messy car can affect more than just your chance for romance. Working our way from the outside in, one welcome benefit of a clean exterior is that it can improve your vehicle's fuel economy — if the car starts out dirty enough, it can see a fuel-efficiency gain approaching 10% once it's been cleaned. And every percentage point counts, given today's fuel prices.

Some road filth can actively damage your car as well. Tree sap and bird poop are prime examples: They can eat right through your vehicle's exterior finish if you don't clean them up promptly. It's a similar story with road salt and other corrosives, which can cause a car to rust if not regularly washed off. Either way, the result can be a cascade of problems. Keep the car, and you could face costly repairs. Try to sell it, and you're likely to get less for a cruddy-looking vehicle than for one that's been freshly detailed. Meanwhile, leaving grime and dust on your windows can turn into a major safety issue if they limit your visibility.

Getting into a car with a disgusting interior can open up its own set of issues. One of the worst is if you drop food or drinks in the cabin and simply leave the spill laying there. Then mold can start forming in your car . Oh, and remember the dead cat in a box mentioned above? Yeah, driving around with dead animals is another bad idea, since they can carry salmonella, hantavirus, e. coli, and more.

article_paragraphs: Dodge will return to the Cup Series after winning the championship in 2012.

Dodge is making a spectacular return to the NASCAR Cup Series next year after leaving the sport at the end of the 2012 season. The company will field a two-car team in the championship alongside Kaulig Racing and will confirm its driver lineup for next year at Homestead-Miami Speedway during this weekend's NASCAR event.

The car manufacturer's return to the sport comes as part of its ongoing recommitment to performance, led by Tim Kuniskis , boss of SRT Performance and Direct Connection in the U.S. Stellantis dipped its toe into NASCAR competition this year by entering the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series and has now committed to a full factory-backed effort in the Cup Series with Dodge SRT Racing. The brand will compete alongside Ford, Chevrolet, and Toyota, making its on-track debut in February during Speedweeks at the Daytona International Speedway.

"Everyone said it was impossible to get back in one year," Kuniskis said when announcing Dodge's return to the sport. "We said, 'watch this.' "Sure, we could spend three years planning, testing and perfecting ... or we could do all three in real time, on the track. It's going to be exponentially harder this way. But slow has never been part of Dodge DNA. LFG."

Dodge last competed in the NASCAR Cup Series in 2012 and claimed the championship with Brad Keselowski. It has secured 217 victories since first joining the Cup Series and, during its most recent tenure from 2001 to 2012, Dodge won 57 races. Remarkably, Dodge will be the first new manufacturer to enter the Cup Series since Toyota did so in 2007. For fans of the sport, it's big news and should add some extra excitement to the championship.

Dodge will unveil its all-new racing car on December 4 at the 2026 Snowball Derby at Five Flags Speedway in Florida. Even if you're not attending, you can livestream the reveal on FloRacing and the NASCAR Channel.

Speaking of Dodge's inclusion in the Cup Series, NASCAR Event Management president John Probst said, "It's something that we've talked about for a long time, and sometimes we talk about it so much and it didn't happen that you almost feel like you lose credibility at some point." He added, "it's certainly a proud moment for us...to welcome Dodge back." If you're not already a NASCAR fan, you should be now.

article_paragraphs: The Illinois Commerce Commission authorized a study of the most affordable way for the state to meet its building decarbonization goals. The report has fundamental flaws but critical insights.

Illinois’s landmark Climate and Equitable Jobs Act (CEJA) sets the goal of 100 percent clean energy across the state by 2050. For nonelectric sources of emissions and transportation—such as the 17 percent of emissions that occur when we burn gas to heat our homes and other buildings where we live, work, and play—CEJA provides little direction on how these sectors are expected to align with the state’s climate goals.

The Illinois Commerce Commission (ICC), which regulates the state’s electric and gas utilities, showed real leadership in 2023 when it found that “if the decarbonization goals of CEJA are to be met, the gas distribution system as currently operated will need to change.” To chart that change, the ICC launched a Future of Gas (FOG) open stakeholder process to identify the most efficient, cost-effective path to a gas system that fits the state’s climate goals.

As part of this FOG process, the ICC authorized a consultant to model five pathways to that CEJA-compliant system by 2050. In its recently released Gas Decarbonization Pathways Study, the consultant modeled a range of scenarios, from one where the state invests heavily in energy efficiency and helps customers replace outdated gas appliances with high-efficiency electric alternatives to others that rely on unproven biofuels with no clear evidence that they can be produced at anything close to the scale needed. For each scenario, the consultant was expected to assess technical feasibility, up-front and operating costs, impacts on the gas and electric systems, emissions reductions, and effects on environmental justice communities, all to help Illinois meet its gas decarbonization goals at the lowest cost and with the most benefits to residents.

Unfortunately, the consultant’s final report is biased by faulty (and at times, plainly unrealistic) assumptions that do not allow for accurate comparison across scenarios. Despite this, the study yields a clear finding: Gas use in Illinois’s buildings and industrial facilities must decline by at least 50 percent in order to reach the state’s climate target of net-zero emissions by 2050. Together with the state’s recently released Comprehensive Climate Action Plan , the study offers Illinois policymakers a clear agenda for initiating the transition to an affordable, equitable, and clean energy future.

The study offers some useful insights, but treating all of its findings as a road map for Illinois’s gas transition would be a mistake. Before getting into the no-regrets steps that Illinois can take now, we need to unpack the biggest problems with the report, including the flawed assumptions behind some of its conclusions.
Despite the study’s shortcomings detailed above, several key findings should influence the recommendations in the final FOG report:

The remaining technologies are incredibly early-stage, and to the extent that they are available at all over the next several decades, they are likely to be extremely expensive. The study’s assumptions around e-methane are particularly troubling. Modeling initially showed that the Continued Gas Use and Hybrid Gas cases could not meet the net-zero-by-2050 emissions requirement using only available technologies, like biomethane. As a result, in the final report, the model selected e-methane to backfill any resource gap—despite the fact that e-methane derived from green hydrogen and direct air carbon capture is still in “prototype and demonstration stage” today.

The report has fundamental flaws but critical insights.

raw_title: They Are Trying to Silence Us
title: They Are Trying to Silence Us
raw_summary: State and federal government officials are trying to harass, intimidate, and silence NRDC and other nonprofit environmental advocates. The Attorney General of West Virginia recently initiated an investigation of NRDC and a handful of other groups on the stated ground that we may have committed consumer fraud. The theory appears to be that it’s deceptive for NRDC to say that the burning of fossil fuels contributes to climate change, which, in turn, causes harm to the planet and its people. But that’s fact, not fraud.
summary: State and federal government officials are trying to harass, intimidate, and silence NRDC and other nonprofit environmental advocates. The Attorney General of West Virginia recently initiated an investigation of NRDC and a handful of other groups on the stated ground that we may have committed consumer fraud.
article_paragraphs: State and federal government officials are trying to harass, intimidate, and silence NRDC and other nonprofit environmental advocates.

The Attorney General of West Virginia recently initiated an investigation of NRDC and a handful of other groups on the stated ground that we may have committed consumer fraud. The theory appears to be that it’s deceptive for NRDC to say that the burning of fossil fuels contributes to climate change, which, in turn, causes harm to the planet and its people. But that’s fact, not fraud.

To pursue his investigation, the AG served a subpoena seeking a vast trove of confidential internal and external communications relating to our advocacy around climate change for the past 10 years. The demand could cover sensitive strategy memos for policy advocacy, draft comments on regulations, exchanges with coalition partners, back-and-forth among scientists, dialogues with donors, and drafts of NRDC publications; all disclosed to a hostile adversary.

Co-counseling with Democracy Forward, we responded to the subpoena by preparing a federal lawsuit asserting infringement of our First Amendment rights to speak, associate with others, and advocate for effective solutions to the climate crisis. Those solutions include the replacement of fossil fuels with renewable sources of energy. And that is what drives the AG’s attempt to punish NRDC: pure retaliation for the content of our point of view.
At 2:13 p.m. on October 22, we advised the AG that we were going to file suit early that evening. A little more than two hours later, at 4:32 p.m., the AG withdrew the subpoena.

The AG is not alone in trying to bully NRDC. In September, the Committee on Natural Resources of the U.S. House of Representatives sent a letter of inquiry to NRDC and 18 other nonprofit environmental groups , informing us they are investigating the groups’ litigation practices. Why? According to the Committee, the targeted groups “build powerful and profitable litigation machines funded by taxpayer dollars through the exploitation of statutory fee-shifting provisions.” On this purported basis, the Committee demanded that NRDC disclose an exhaustive array of intrusive information and documents that could take months of concentrated effort to produce.

The premise of the Committee’s inquiry is that NRDC “effectively function[s] as [a] law firm[] funded by taxpayer dollars.” It calls NRDC “one of the most active litigating environmental nonprofit organizations driving the exploitation of statutory fee–shifting provisions.”

While NRDC is indeed an active litigant in federal court, it rarely receives attorney fees from the federal government. During our past five fiscal years, NRDC’s income from such fees in cases involving agencies or statutes identified in the Committee’s letter constituted 0.112 percent of our operating budget. In light of this numerical fact, contending that NRDC “build[s] a business model focused on siphoning tax dollars by weaponizing litigation awards” is unmoored from reality. With minimal effort, Committee members or staff could have discovered this from documents in the public record.

article_paragraphs: PHOENIX — Arizona utilities Tucson Electric Power Company (TEP) and Arizona Public Service (APS) filed their 2026 Integrated Resource Plans (IRPs) on Friday that evaluate how utilities will obtain energy for the next 15 years. While their plans include new renewable energy and storage, they continue to spend on fossil fuels, building new gas, and in the case of APS, extending coal use. Instead of facilitating a timely transition to affordable, clean energy, both utilities — and especially APS — continue an expensive dependence on fossil fuels that keep ratepayers in a dangerous cycle, paying the price for decades.

Arizonans already experience some of the highest electric bills in the country, with some of the most planned gas in the country. Yet, instead of easing energy burden and saving its customers millions of dollars, APS prolongs costly coal operations at the Four Corners coal plant, worsening climate impacts, increasing air pollution, and threatening public health.

Of all the state’s utilities, APS has the most planned fossil gas , adding over 4,000 MW of gas by 2041. APS’s gas projects include the planned Desert Sun Power Plant and the Redhawk Expansion Project, which includes constructing eight new methane gas-fired generating turbines in Maricopa County. It has also signed a coal supply contract extension to resuscitate its Four Corners Plant , abandoning APS’s previous plan to exit the plant in 2031 and instead extending coal-fired operations to 2038. In a pending case before the Arizona Corporation Commission, APS is also proposing a 14% rate hike that would increase the average residential customer’s utility bill by roughly $240 per year.

TEP’s energy plan includes coal to gas conversions of units 1 and 2 at its Springerville plant by 2031 rather than retirement of those units as TEP had previously proposed. TEP plans to exit its share of the Four Corners coal plant by 2031, but also plans to add 300 MW of new fossil gas generation. TEP had previously committed to reduce carbon emissions 80 percent by 2035 but now says in its plan that it won’t achieve that goal.
The public can submit comments on both utility energy plans. Both APS and TEP’s plans will come before the Arizona Corporation Commission to be approved or rejected.

“Arizonans across the state support a timely transition from fossil fuels to 100% clean energy by 2050, but what the utilities have presented in their energy plans further delays our move from gas and coal to solar and wind,” said Sierra Club Grand Canyon Chapter Director Sandy Bahr . “We’re seeing these utilities protect their own bottom lines, instead of making the most economical decisions for ratepayers like you and me. More than ever, we need to embrace a clean energy future to protect our health, the climate, and our wallets.”

Passport Hub handles the connections between charging networks and the services drivers use, including exchanging session information and settling payments. That lets a charging operator connect to multiple services through a single integration.

In practice, ChargeHub users can pull up a bp pulse location, select a port, and start charging from their existing account. The app displays the charging cost and wallet balance, and drivers need funds in their ChargeHub wallet to begin charging.
ChargeHub also shows real-time charger availability and lets drivers filter by connector type. Its bp pulse guide says most of the network’s chargers use CCS, with a growing share offering NACS.

Meanwhile, bp pulse has been adding physical charging sites, too. Recent openings include 12 charging bays at a TravelCenters of America location in Grand Bay, Alabama, and 22 bays near Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.

Before starting a session, check the price shown in the app. ChargeHub’s guide notes that its Plus subscription waives activation fees, so using an existing account doesn’t necessarily mean paying the same total as another payment method.
